The tornado started near the Calcasieu River near Mike Manuel Road. As it moved northeast, a tree was blown into a manufactured home and the front porch awning was ripped off. Another home had a damaged carport which fell onto a car. Several softwood trees were snapped off at the tops with a couple of hardwood trees snapped off near their bases. A third small industrial building on the property sustained damage to its roll-up shop door and a nearby parked and loaded construction trailer was pushed 4 to 6 feet to the east. The tornado lifted after this point, although its |circulation remained close to the surface as noted by bent and snapped softwood trees down Mike Manuel Road. The maximum estimated winds were 111 mph.
A barn was damaged along with a carport.
Heavy rain flooded streets in portions of Groves. Water was reported to be at least 1 foot deep over Twin City Highway near Thomas Jefferson Middle School.
Wind gusts downed multiple trees around the town of Burkeville.
A high wind gust downed a tree onto a highway in Oretta.
Heavy rain flooded sections of a roadway southwest of Ville Platte.

Numerous roads in Evangeline Parish near Ville Platte were closed due to flooding.

An EF-1 tornado touched down near 10th street on the northwest edge of Forest Hill. The tornado tracked northeast across Highway 165 and lifted near Fish Hatchery Road.  Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. There was also extensive damage to a nursery and a home located at the nursery. Several outbuildings were also heavily damaged. The maximum estimated winds were 105 mph.

An EF-1 tornado touched down roughly 2 miles south of Woodworth near Campground Road and tracked northeast across Interstate 49 and lifted just east of Old Baton Rouge Highway. The tornado damaged vehicles and buildings at the Louisiana Department of Agriculture and Forestry, while snapping and uprooting numerous trees. The tornado then heavily damaged a large office supply building located on Highway 167. The tornado then damaged a home and numerous outbuildings at a farm on Old Baton Rouge Highway prior to lifting just northeast of this location. The maximum estimated winds were 110 mph.

A storm spotter photographed a tornado that briefly touched down in the Coulee Teal Swamp. The NWS attempted to survey this tornado, however, there are no roads into the area where the tornado touched down. Therefore, the rating will remain unknown.
An EF-1 tornado briefly touched down in an area along Bayou Benoit Levee Road. A mobile home was flipped over, while a few trees sustained damage. Maximum estimated winds were 95 mph.

An EF-2 tornado touched down just southwest of New Iberia, and tracked northeast along the southeastern edge of New Iberia. The tornado damaged roughly 20 to 25 mobile homes on Bradley Lane. Four of these mobile homes were completely destroyed. ||The tornado then tracked northeast through mostly open field, and clipped a neighborhood on Fontelieu Drive and Copper Road. ||The tornado then directly impacted the New Iberia Medical Center. Numerous vehicles and buildings in the medical center district were heavily damaged. The roofing exterior was completely blown off of a mid rise medical building. A large chunk of the roof decking was also ripped off, while some interior wall damage occurred. ||The tornado then heavily damaged numerous homes along Bayou BLVD, Avenue Bonne Terre, and Old Jeanerette Road.  The tornado continued northeast over open field, before lifting near Sam Snead Drive. ||Maximum estimated winds were 135 mph.
This is the Satellite tornado visible on the video footage and verified the location using satellite imagery in a field just west of highway 83.
Heavy rain caused Little Pine Island to go over bank full and flood streets around Pinewood Estates.
Stream gages indicated multiple bayous or ditches overflowed in China and Hampshire. Numerous roads were also flooded by several inches of rain in west Jefferson County.

Several pine trees were damaged along with a few hardwoods. The tornado reached maximum intensity near County Road 4600 where a few pine trees were snapped within it's trunk. At this same location, a BBQ shack was heavily damaged along with an awning that was completely destroyed. A pontoon boat was ripped off of its trailer, and thrown approximately 25 yards into a pine tree. Two mobile homes also sustained minor damage along County Road 4600. Estimated maximum winds were 90 mph.
A flagpole was snapped and leaning on a home.
Saint Landry EOC reported road closures due to heavy rain flooding streets.
A metal shed had half its roof removed by high winds and a portion of a carport roof was also torn off.

Widespread street flooding was reported in Lafayette. Between five and six inches of rain fell across northern Lafayette Parish.

An EF-1 tornado began along Pershing Loftin Road and moved east through the Shear community before ending near Williams Road. The main damage was to trees, but one barn lost part of its roof and a home on Pine Ridge Road lost some shingles. On Willie Hargrove Road, several large trees were blown down, and one mobile home that was tied down was destroyed. Two people received minor injuries.
An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down south of DeRidder on Highway 171. Several trees were blown down or uprooted.
An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down on Raoul Road, destroying one barn and blowing down several trees.

An EF-0 tornado began southwest of the LA 92/LA 343 intersection near Maurice, and moved northeast into Lafayette Parish. In Vermilion Parish, the tornado destroyed one mobile home and moved another one off its blocks. In the Adola subdivision, several homes lost shingles or vinyl siding. Several trees were also blown down.

This is a continuation of the tornado that began west of Maurice in Vermilion Parish. It strengthened to EF-2 intensity before dissipating a mile west of the Acadiana Mall. Near the Duhon and West Broussard Road intersection, one permanent home had the roof completely blown off, hitting the neighboring house and causing extensive damage. The two people inside the roof-less home escaped injury. Other homes along the path received minor roof or siding damage, and many trees were blown down.

An EF-0 tornado touched down just east of the Ambassador Caffery and Kaliste Saloom intersection, and moved through the Beaullieu Place and River Ranch subdivisions. Scattered trees were blown down and some shingles were blown off several homes.

An EF-0 tornado touched down in the Theall community, and moved east before dissipating near the shipyard on Highway 690. Along the way, many trees were blown down. A few homes received minor damage to their roof or siding.

An EF-1 tornado began near the Oil Center area of Lafayette. Several medical buildings received significant roof damage with debris from the roofs knocking out windows in neghboring buidlings. Trees and power poles were blown down, damaging some parked cars.

An EF-1 tornado formed behind the Wal-Mart in Breaux Bridge and moved south along Highway 328, damaging several large warehouses. The tornado moved across Highway 94, destroying an insurance business and damaging several homes and apartments near it. The storm turned more to the left, and headed south through Beaux Bridge, blowing down many trees and causing more damage to homes and businesses. The tornado dissipated southeast of Breaux Bridge along Huval Road where it shifted a home off its pilings, injuring one man inside.

After receiving four to six inches of rain, some homes had water enter them in the Oakborne subdivision, and along Pinhook Road, Evangeline Thruway, and 10th Street.
After receiving four to six inches of rain, Highway 29 between Chataignier and Ville Platte flooded.
After receiving four to six inches of rain, several roadways in St. Landry Parish flooded, including Highway 182 and 190 near Opelousas, LA 93 near Arnaudville, and US 190 near Lawtell.

Trees were blown down around Kirbyville.
Power poles were snapped in Beauxart Gardens. Southeast Texas Regional Airport also recorded a wind gust of 55 mph.
A large tree was downed onto a roof in Port Acres.
Multiple homes suffered damage from high wind gusts.

The Orange-Calcasieu Tornado touched down near Orangefield Road and quickly produced EF-2 damage a few blocks northwest of Orangefield High School. This area sustained the most severe damage from this tornado, where winds were estimated to max out at 120 mph. Numerous homes were either heavily damaged or destroyed. The tornado then crossed over Cow Bayou, and produced mostly EF-1 damage through the rest of Orange County.  The tornado crossed the Sabine River over a section of West Bluff Road. A marine survey revealed that the tornado did remain continuous across the Sabine River Swamp area.

A brief tornado developed over the Bessie Heights Marsh producing damage to trees and roofs from Nora Circle across Round Bunch Road, Edgar Drive to Turner Road. The tornado damaged electrical transmission lines as it weakened before Bessie Heights Road. Max estimated winds were 100 mph.

An EF-1 tornado touched down just south of Highway 73, and tracked into the Taylor Landing community. Weak damage to roofs were common, along with uprooted trees and destroyed privacy fences. The tornado ended somewhere in the Taylor Bayou marsh downstream from Taylor Landing. Max estimated winds were 90 mph.
Water rose above bank full on drainage ditches north of Buna flooding area roads.
Boggy Creek exceeded bank full flooding adjacent areas near Lumberton.
Streets were flooded and cars were stalled due to heavy rain.
A mesonet site recorded a wind gust of 64 mph.
Roads were closed in Crowley due to flooding.
A NWS employee reported street flooding in Carnecro.
The Gum Slough Tornado touched down just south of Line Road, and merged with the Nibletts Bluff Tornado. Trees were damaged while sections of roofs were taken off of a mobile home and an outbuilding.

An EF-2 tornado touched down near near Perkins Pipeline Road and tracked northeast for 12 miles through northern Calcasieu Parish and into southeast Beauregard Parish. Only 4 miles were in Calcasieu Parish and the tornado only damaged trees and power lines before tracking into Beauregard Parish. Max estimated winds were 125 mph.

A National Weather Service storm survey revealed that an EF-1 tornado touched down near Jackson Gimnick Loop and tracked northeast into rural southeast Beauregard Parish. This tornado lifted prior to reaching the Allen Parish line. This tornado tracked mostly through open fields or forested areas. There were some homes and outbuildings damaged along Foreman Road and near Doug Addison Road. Maximum estimated winds were 100 mph.
Siding was removed from a home on Boudreaux Lane and large branches were broken from a tree on CalCam Line Road.
A tractor trailer was overturned on Interstate 10.
Lake Charles Regional Airport recorded a wind gust of 51 knots.
A mesonet station in Opelousas recorded a wind gust of 63 mph.

This tornado is a continuation from the Orange Tornado. The tornado crossed the Sabine River near a section of West Bluff Road and the Sabine River Swamp area eventually impacting the Niblett's Bluff Park in Calcasieu Parish, Louisiana. The tornado gained strength once again, destroying homes, RVs, and other outbuildings along Wright Road. The tornado then produced mostly EF1 damage through the remainder of it's path into the Sabine River Diversion System, and the Big Woods area. |The tornado finally lifted near Woods Loop Road just north of it's intersection with Navaho Trail. Max estimated winds were 120 mph.

This tornado developed in Calcasieu Parish and continued into Beauregard Parish. The tornado damaged numerous homes and outbuildings, while snapping or uprooting numerous trees. This tornado tracked directly through the community of Gaytine after crossing Highway 171. There were three injuries with this tornado prior to lifting east of the Gaytine community. Maximum estimated winds were 125 mph.

The tornado started near Lyons Point Hwy and Kite Rd before continuing southeast rapidly. Roughly 8 outbuildings were destroyed along a subdivision on Sally Road. The Tiger Island Wildfire began between Merryville, DeRidder, and Singer and affected mostly pine forest. The area affected had ample dry fuels from the exceptional drought and downed trees from Hurricane Laura. The fire spread to over 31,000 acres and caused evacuations of Merryville and a portion of Singer and DeRidder. Approximately 7 homes and 39 structures altogether burned.

Four main wildfires occurred in Vernon Parish at the end of August with over 9,000 acres burned. One home and multiple outbuildings were burned in the Ida Fire with approximately 3,628 acres affected. The Highway 113 Fire was along the Vernon and Rapides Parish line with more than half inside of Vernon Parish. It burned just over 7,124 acres burned in total of pine forest. The Lion's Camp Road Fire did not destroy any homes, however 785 acres burned of pine forest. The Miller Fire was along the Sabine River and burned over 1.300 acres of forest.

Two main wildfires occurred during the end of August in Rapides Parish. The Elizabeth fire burned one home and roughly 940 acres of pine forest while the Claiborne Fire burned 1,600 acres of pine forest.

Rain finally moved across Beauregard Parish early in the month helping to contain the Tiger Island Wildfire. The fire burned 31,290 acres and numerous structures during August with no significant growth or burned structures in September.

First noticeable damage was near Sandhill Road Southeast of the intersection with Joe Smith Road. It intersected Joe Smith Road and Crossed Cora Road. The last visible damage is near the end of J Harper Road. Only tree damage was noted. Maximum estimated wind speed was 80 mph.

A weak tornado touched down just west of Forest Road 212 and moved east southeast across Oden Lake producing minor tree damage. The damage ends just to the east of HWY 165. Maximum estimated winds were 75 mph.

The tornado started along North Lee St (just south of the intersection with Tarleton St) with damage to trees, power lines, and roofs. The path continued across HWY 107 where nearby homes sustained damage to roofs from tree branches. Further east, damage from the tornado also occurred along the southern periphery of the track north of Andrus St where an oak tree fell through a small home. Thereafter the tornado continued over Spring Bayou Golf Course and progressed along an ENE motion toward rural lands south of Pecan Dr and River Ln. It continued east ending near the Lake Ophelia National Wildlife Refuge.

The tornado began over northeast Cottonport near the intersection of Lana Street and Zion Street where homes sustained substantial roof and carport damage while multiple tree branches were scattered. The path continued along a NE motion over rural lands while cross Couvillion Street. Further tree damage and debris was found in nearby farmland along the tornado path. Later the path crossed MP Cutoff Road near Mill Bayou with damage of large tree trunks seen nearby. Southeast of Hamburg the tornado uprooted more trees south of Coco Lake. Hereafter, the tornado took a ENE motion starting along HWY 451 crossing Sutton Lake. After a 15 mile track the tornado ended near a cemetery along HWY 451 and Big Bend Road where further tree damage and the collapse of an old home was found. Maximum winds were estimated at 105 mph.

A NWS storm survey revealed that an EF-2 tornado impacted areas of Port Arthur. The tornado began near the intersection of 17th Street and Savannah Ave southeast of Motiva. The tornado path traveled east, peaking out near the Progressive Missionary Baptist Church where a large portion of the masonry walls collapsed. Another home near 11th Street and Orange Ave had the roof completely removed and some walls collapsed. Home and tree damage was extensive across these neighborhoods in Port Arthur. The path continued across Rose Hill Park and onto Pleasure Island. The tornado likely continued into Sabine Lake. Maximum estimated winds were 120 mph.

The tornado began near the intersection of Herbert Camp Rd and Big Pasture Road, resulting in EF0-EF1 tree damage as it headed northeast.  Surging winds to the south of the tornadic circulation removed the roof of an outbuilding farther east down Big Pasture Rd. The tornado continued northeast through marshy and uninhabited areas, crossing the Intracoastal waterway south of the Grand Lake Swing Bridge.  To the south of LA-384, an untethered mobile home was flipped and destroyed.  On the north side of the highway, an RV and a small outbuilding were overturned. The tornado continued east-northeast, causing additional tree damage as it neared and crossed Gulf Highway. |The tornado caused additional tree damage as it passed through the Vincent Road and Piccou Lane area before dissipating shortly after.

A tornado touched down near Vernon road on the eastern side of McNeese State University and crossed Common, Center, Harvard and Kirkman streets before moving into the Moss Memorial Health Complex causing damage to roofing. The tornado continued across Louisiana Ave where it further intensified destroying the roofs of several homes along Elton Court while also causing widespread tree and electrical damage. The tornado weakened as it crossed Brentwood lane before dissipating just east of Walton Street. Maximum estimated winds were 115 mph.

The tornado touched down to the south of LA-384 near Honore Lane, damaging trees as it headed northeast toward the Intracoastal waterway.  The tornado continued through generally marshy and uninhabited areas until nearing Gulf Highway to the south of b1BANK, causing additional tree damage and tearing off a metal awning from a storage building and tossing it approximately 300 feet into a neighboring yard. The tornado then crossed Gulf Highway, leaning wooden utility poles toward the east, and|dissipating in a field to the southeast of the bank. Max estimated winds were 100 mph.

The tornado touched down just northeast of Bayou Courtableau, causing tree damage and minor roof damage to residential homes on Vista Drive. One carport was destroyed. The tornado continued northeast across Camp Thistlethwaite and I-49 causing additional tree damage. The tornado reached LA-182 where utility poles were leaned over before it dissipated in an open field east of LA-182 and north of Plant Rd. Maximum estimated winds were 95 mph.

A brief tornado touched down on a property to the west of West Todd Rd, destroying a sheet metal carport, causing overhang/fascia damage to a home and tree damage. The tornado continued northeast crossing W Todd Road and an open field, reaching a property to the west of LA-27 causing additional tree damage and overturning an unanchored wooden storage barn prior to dissipating. Maximum estimated winds were estimated at 100 mph.

The Tornado began east of LA-101 along Ardoin Cove Road, causing damage to trees and a mobile home. A metal building had part of its roof removed, which was thrown into a field. The tornado moved east-northeast, crossing Parish Road 720A and causing damage to utility poles, then crossing LA-1131 causing damage to trees and mobile homes. The tornado continued east-northeast toward LeBlanc Road causing damage to several metal outbuildings, then passed through agricultural fields before crossing Abell|Road west of East Bayou Lacassine. A National Weather Service storm survey revealed that an EF-2 tornado impacted areas near Jasper, Texas. The tornado touched down somewhere in the Little Walnut Run Valley and tracked 8.6 miles to the northwest lifting somewhere in the Indian Creek|Valley.  The tornado also tracked through the west side of the city of Jasper.  Numerous power poles and trees were snapped or uprooted. Numerous homes and outbuildings were heavily damaged. The tornado weakened as it crossed Highway 190 in Jasper, only to regain EF-2 strength as it crossed Houston Street in a wooded area. There was one injury associated with this tornado. The maximum estimated winds were 115 mph.

The tornado crossed Highway 190 and directly hit a meat market where 3 people were injured. A cinder block wall fell over as roughly 25 percent of the roofing material was pulled off the building. An old barn was also damaged behind the meat market. The tornado was weakening as it crossed Stagg Avenue where there was minor tree damage along with damage to a couple of power poles. Maximum estimated winds were 95 mph.

The tornado touched down just west of Ben Road. It moved northeast where it destroyed a garage, a mobile home shifted off its foundation, and part of a roof was removed from a home. An old frame home was completely destroyed. The tornado continued to move northeast and crossed Fats Rd leaving debris across the roadway. The tornado then moved into Acadia Parish as it crossed Bayou Queue de Tortue. Maximum estimated winds were 105 mph.

Tide levels at Sabine Pass reached 2.03 feet above MHHW at time of high tide during the evening of the 18th. This caused minor flooding of Highway 87 between Sabine Pass and Port Arthur.
The tide level at Cameron reached 2.01 feet above MHHW at high tide. This caused minor flooding on Highway 82 near the courthouse for a few hours.

Strong south winds ahead of a cold front and the remnants of Rafael in the gulf produced high tides along the coast of Cameron Parish. The tide level reached 2.1 feet above MHHW which produced minor flooding of Highway 82 near the Cameron Courthouse.

Strong south winds ahead of a cold front and the remnants of Rafael in the gulf produced high tides along the coast of Cameron Parish. The tide level reached 2.1 feet above MHHW which produced minor flooding of Highway 82 near Holly Beach and some secondary roads in Holly Beach.

Strong south winds ahead of a cold front and the remnants of Rafael in the gulf produced high tides along the coast of Vermilion Parish. The tide level reached 2.88 feet above MHHW at the Freshwater Lock. This produced minor flooding near the lock.

Strong south winds ahead of a cold front and the remnants of Rafael in the gulf produced high tides along the coast of Jefferson County. The tide level reached 2.1 feet above MHHW which produced minor flooding of Highway 87 between Sabine Pass and Port Arthur. Minor flooding also occurred at Sea Rim State Park from high surf.

Six RVs were flipped along the west bank of Sabine Lake on Pleasure Island. Two people were injured. This was caused by strong winds flowing into the approaching tornadic supercell that would pass to the south of the RV park.

An EF-3 tornado developed south of Houston and moved across Chambers County into Jefferson County just south of Russel Road. It snapped off power poles at French Rd before continuing northeast. An area of trees were snapped off and uprooted just south of the Big Hill Strategic Oil Reserve. The tornado continued northeast where it destroyed the top floor of the Sabine Ranch Lodge, stripped metal from a nearby industrial building, flipped a car into a side yard, and damaged the roofs of two homes. The car contained two people, one sustained a minor injury. The tornado crossed Highways 87 and 82 where it snapped transmission poles. Finally, it moved overtop Sabine Lake. The track continued into western Cameron Parish. Maximum winds were estimated at 161 mph.
Golf ball size hail was reported at the Pleasure Island RV resort just before winds flipped multiple RVs.

A long lived tornado moved across Jefferson County and Sabine Lake into Cameron Parish. Satellite imagery and radar indicated TDSs showed the tornado moved into marsh near Willow Bayou and dissipated in the Sabine National Wildlife Refuge near Five Lakes.
Multiple reports were received of minor street flooding in Pineville and Alexandria.
Pictures were received of street flooding in Leesville.

Several pine trees were uprooted across Lookout Road during the beginning of the Brushy Creek Tornado. A radar tornado debris signature was associated with this damage. The tornado crossed Highway 463 producing pine tree damage at EF-0 strength and dissipated after passing the roadway. The path was not fully surveyed between Lookout road and Highway 463 due to ammunitions zone within Fort Johnson. Maximum estimated winds were 90 mph.

Tree and power line damage occurred as the tornado moved across Highway 465. The small tornado damaged several trees and a frame home. One outbuilding was destroyed. Tornado strengthened in this area of Ian Johnson Road. The tornado crossed Cutts Road damaging numerous trees and then dissipated. Maximum estimated winds were 100 mph.

The Wilda Tornado began off of Saint Clair Road and Kevin Lane where several trees were snapped and a small shed had its metal roof torn off. A tornado debris signature was associated with this damage. The tornado then continued north-northeast along Saint Clair Road, intermittently touching down. Damage is weak and narrow along this part of the path and is confined to minor tree damage. From there the tornado crossed Saint Clair Rd and continued northeast, eventually crossing Browns Creek Rd. At this location a metal outbuilding was completely destroyed and thrown roughly 100 yards downstream with the tornado. A table was thrown roughly 300 yards west northwest of where it was placed. Minor damage to a frame home also occurred at the end point of the Wilda Tornado.

The tornado started just south of Old Seale Road to the west of HWY 27. The tornado moved northeast crossing HWY 27. Then across George Kendall Road just east of Billy White Road. The only notable damage was snapped trees. Maximum estimated winds were 90 mph.

The tornado began off of Cooper Church Road near the community of Savage Fork where several trees were damaged near Bayou Castor. The tornado then moved east-northeast where it crossed Fletcher Road. The damage path in this area is intermittent in nature, but is associated with a tornado debris signature. The tornado then made a more east-southeast turn and crossed Hazel Jeans Road where weak tree damage was found. This damage is also associated with a tornado debris signature. The tornado then continued southeast, crossing Hwy 171, and continuing onward where it crossed a dirt road and damaged more trees. Beyond the dirt road, the tornado continued off into a thick brush/forested area where it eventually lifted. Maximum estimated winds were 90 mph.

The tornado began just east of Highway 171 where it pulled a roof and metal panels off of an outbuilding/shed type structure.  Nearby, just to the southeast, the tornado caused minor roof damage to two homes, pulling several shingles off. The tornado then continued southeast, crossing Eissman Road and snapping several pine trees.  From there, it continued southeast and moved into Fort Johnson, causing minor softwood tree damage before dissipating. Maximum estimated winds were 80 mph.

The tornado began around 1/2 mile north of Fullerton Lake, in a heavily wooded, inaccessible area. The tornado then continued southeast, cross Fullerton Lake Road where it snapped around 40 to 50 trees near the entrance to the Fullerton Lake Rec Complex. From there, the tornado continued southeast into to more heavily wooded areas, eventually lifting before it crossed any other roads. Maximum estimated winds were 100 mph.

A tornado briefly touched down and crossed Jeff McDonald Road in far eastern Vernon Parish. Several trees were found to have been snapped and/or uprooted in a convergence pattern along this point in the road. The tornado was likely very brief, as no other damage was found on surrounding roads.

Tornado started in the St. Landry community where it damaged and snapped some hardwood trees. It moved across Interstate 49 and into Saint Landry Parish. The maximum wind speed was estimated at 95 mph.

Satellite and radar analyses indicate a tornado touched down south west of Sweet Lake. The tornado moved northeast towards Sweet Lake where a very marked and narrow corridor of damage to vegetation could be seen. This portion of the damage path coincides with maximum intensity of a radar observed tornado debris signature. Damage to vegetation continued east of Sweet Lake as the tornado crossed the Intracoastal Waterway. Damage becomes sparse between the waterway and HWY 27 where the tornado dissipated.

The tornado began roughly 0.5 miles west of HWY 287 where several trees were damaged along with some outbuildings. The tornado then continued northeast where it damaged a home, an outbuilding was destroyed, and several pine trees were snapped at the trunk. Two by fours were impaled into the roof of the home as well. Roughly 30% of roof was peeled off of the home. The tornado then continued east towards HWY 287 where tree damage was found near Little Cypress Creek.  This was the end of the Little Cypress Tornado. Max estimated wind was 95 mph.

The Boyce Tornado began in a field to the southwest of I-49 in Rapides Parish, where powerlines were removed from transmission towers. The tornado continued northeast crossing I-49 and damaged homes as it crossed HWY 1.  It proceeded northeast into the town of Boyce, damaging several more homes, destroying outbuildings, and damaging various trees in the middle of Boyce. The tornado then continued further northeast, crossing the Red River into Shreveport's CWA. Weak tree occurred on the north side of the Red River in Grant Parish, until it lifted around 11:57 AM. Max estimated winds were 90 mph.

Minor tree damage was also noted on the property.|Several pine trees were snapped off on S Jeane Rd. Pine tree damage was noted on Fal Rd were the tornado crossed the roadway. The tornado touched down west of Hwy 14 on Pinewood Drive where minor damage was observed to mobile homes. It continued southeast across HWY 14, damaging several large live oak trees near Walden drive. A home sustained roof damage when the tornado ripped the awning from the home on Wilson Drive. Several homes and outbuildings received minor damage as the tornado exited the neighborhood to the southeast. Max estimated winds were 90 mph.

The tornado started just east of 108 and just south of the Vincent Settlement Elementary School and crossed over Oak Lake Drive just north of Moss Lake where mostly tree damage and minor siding damage was observed. The tornado crossed the ship channel and went across the north portion of Gray Plantation and crossed over Big Lake Road, where trees and an overturned shed was observed. The tornado ended just east of Elliot Road where significant shingle damage was observed. Before the Rear flank downdraft winds overwhelmed the tornadic circulation. The observed damage to the south and east was from the rear flank down draft with winds estimated in the 60 to 80 MPH range.

Damage was noted to the east where the tornado crossed Crooked Creek Pkwy, where further tree damage was noted.

Between 4 and 5 inches of rain fell in less than 3 hours, resulting in street flooding of sections of Lafayette.

Over ten inches of rain fell in sections of New Iberia, resulting in widespread flooding of streets, and even some homes. The hardest hit areas were the West End, and Shelton, Spencer Loop, Anderson, Lombard, and Elizabeth Streets.
Over ten inches of rain fell through the overnight hours in northwestern sections of Avoyelles Parish. Besides flooded roads, a nursing home was evacuated in Effie.

Over ten inches of rain fell overnight in Alexandria and Pineville, resulting in widespread urban flooding. Over 200 water rescues were performed where people were trapped in their homes filling with water, and at least 1000 autos were flooded. At least 450 homes and 150 businesses were flooded.
Significant street flooding was reported in Egan due to at least 4 inches of rain falling in less than 3 hours.
Between 4 and 5 inches of rain fell in less than 3 hours, resulting in street flooding of sections of Breaux Bridge.

Between 6 and 10 inches of rain fell in less than 3 hours, resulting in serious street flooding between Woodworth and Glenmora. Some people were evacuated due to rising water, including a nursing home.
Between 6 and 8 inches of rain fell in less than 3 hours, resulting in serious street flooding between Opelousas and Washington.
A small tornado was seen by a trained spotter near Effie. It produced no damage.
A small tornado was seen by a sheriff deputy near Mansura. It produced no damage.
A tornado caused minor roof damage to three homes near Leblanc. Eyewitnesses could hear the tornado snapping trees.

A strong tornado began near Duralde, and ended near Mamou. Along the way, a home on Valentine Road lost part of its roof, causing one minor injury. A home of Highway 374 was severely damaged when it was knocked off its foundation. Along Duculus Road, two homes lost most of their roofs. One unoccupied, tied-down mobile home was tossed to the northwest over 100 yards and split in half. Another mobile home was thrown in a counter-clockwise motion over 200 yards and was destroyed, resulting in two fatalities and one serious injury. Near the end of the path on Highway 104, a home lost part of its roof. Numerous trees and power lines were blown down along the path.
A tornado briefly touched down near the sheriff department in Crowley. The primary damage was blown down trees and some garbage cans thrown around.
A tornado briefly touched down near Highway 31 south of Hebert Road, where several large trees were blown down and a mobile home lost its roof.
A tornado briefly touched down in Cheneyville, resulting in minor damage to roofs of several homes and businesses.

Hurricane Gustav moved across St. Mary Parish, damaging thousands of homes and businesses. Hardest hit areas were the Morgan City and Patterson areas.In Morgan City, the water plant, steam plant, and electric plant were damaged. In Franklin an elementary school lost part of the roof. While the wind damage was severe, it was not as bad as Hurricane Andrew in 1992.

Hurricane Gustav moved across Iberia Parish, damaging thousands of homes and businesses. The hardest hit area was New Iberia. Some homes with metal roofs had them peeled back. At least 23,000 customers lost power.

Hurricane Gustav moved across lower St. Martin Parish, damaging homes and businesses. The hardest hit area was Stephensville. The school had two air conditioners blow off the roof, and a radio tower next to the school lost the top 20-30 feet of the tower.

Hurricane Gustav moved across upper St. Martin Parish, damaging over 1000 homes and businesses. The hardest hit areas were Breaux Bridge to St. Martinville. A St. Martinville woman died in a house fire caused by a candle.
Hurricane Gustav moved across Lafayette Parish, damaging some homes and businesses. One man was killed when a tree fell through his roof of the house he was living in.
Hurricane Gustav moved across Evangeline Parish, causing widespread wind dmaage with trees and power lines blown down parish-wide. The hospital roof in Ville Platte was blown off.

Hurricane Gustav moved across Evangeline Parish, causing widespread wind damage with trees and power lines blown down parish-wide. The hardest hit areas were between Washington, Nubia, Sunset, and Grand Coteau, where large trees were blown down. In Opelousas, the high school lost part of its roof and a wall partially collapsed. Several other schools in the parish received roof damage to the gyms, auditoriums, and cafeterias. This was worse wind damage than Hurricane Lili in 2002.
Hurricane Gustav weakend across eastern sections of Allen Parish, yet widespread trees and power lines were blwon down.
Hurricane Gustav moved across Avoyelles Parish, causing wind damage between Bunkie and Marksville.

Hurricane Gustav caused widespread trees and power lines downed across Rapides Parish. Some of the worst wind damage was in Forest Hill, Glenmora, Cheneyville, and Woodworth. At the Alexandria Mall, part of the roof caved in, damaging many stores in the mall.
Hurricane Gustav moved across northeastern Acadia Parish, causing widespread wind damage with trees and power lines blown down. Church Point was the hardest hit area.
Hurricane Gustav caused tropical storm force winds in Jeff Davis Parish, resulting in scattered trees and power lines downed.

Hurricane Gustav caused tropical storm force winds in Calcasieu Parish, resulting in scattered trees and power lines downed, mainly between DeQuincy, Moss Bluff, and Iowa. Two men died from carbon monoxide poisoning when they improperly placed a running generator inside their home.
Hurricane Gustav caused tropical storm force winds in Cameron Parish, resulting in scattered trees and power lines downed, mainly east of Grand Chenier.
Hurricane Gustav caused tropical storm force winds in Vermilion Parish, resulting in scattered trees and power lines downed, mainly in eastern sections of the parish.
Hurricane Gustav caused tropical storm force winds in Vernon Parish, resulting in scattered trees and power lines downed, mainly in Pitkin and Cravens areas.
Hurricane Gustav caused tropical storm force winds in Beauregard Parish, resulting in scattered trees and power lines downed.
Hurricane Ike had wind gust speeds of 80-90 mph in western sections of Cameron Parish, resulting in wind damage to homes and businesses in the Johnson Bayou to Cameron areas.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph, resulting in minor wind damage across Acadia Parish.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph, resulting in minor wind damage across Allen Parish.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph, resulting in wind damage across Beauregard Parish.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph, resulting in wind damage across Calcasieu Parish, mainly across western sections.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph, resulting in minor wind damage across Iberia Parish.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph, resulting in minor wind damage across Jeff Davis Parish.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph, resulting in minor wind damage across St. Mary Parish.
Hurricane Ike caused tropical storm wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph, resulting in minor wind damage across Vermilion Parish.

Hurricane Ike resulted in a 12 foot storm surge along the coast in Cameron Parish, slightly smaller than Hurricane Rita in 2005. At least 3000 homes were flooded. Many modular and mobile homes that were not elevatetd were destroyed by the storm surge. Water rescues were performed in Grand Lake and Hackberry.

Hurricane Ike resulted in an 11 foot storm surge along the Calcasieu River, slightly higher than Hurricane Rita in 2005. At least 1000 homes were flooded, including in the city of Lake Charles, Westlake, and Sulphur. Southern sections of the parish, including Black Bayou, also flooded homes.
Hurricane Ike resulted in a 10 foot storm surge up the Mermentau River, flooding a few homes in Lake Arthur.

Hurricane Ike resulted in a 7-8 foot storm surge, similar to Hurricane Rita in 2005. Homes and businesses along and south of Highway 14 and Highway 90 had water enter them. This included the Port of Iberia. Over 1000 homes were flooded. A bridge was damaged when a barge rain into it near Weeks Island.
Hurricane Ike resulted in a 7-8 foot storm surge, similar to Hurricane Rita in 2005. Roads in the Stephensville area had water over them, but little came into the houses.

Hurricane Ike resulted in a 7-9 foot storm surge, similar to Hurricane Rita in 2005. At Cypremort Point, homes and camps not elevated were severely damaged. Water was 3 to 6 feet deep across the road. A man-made levee along the Franklin Canal failed in Franklin, flooding hundreds of homes and a nursing home. Parish-wide, over 450 homes were flooded.
Storm surge reached into southern sections of Acadia Parish, causing minor flooding.
A tornado briefly touched down in the fields northeast of Arnaudville, causing no damage.
A tornado briefly touched down near Gueydan in a field, doing no damage.
Ham radio operators reported a tornado touch down with no damage.
Ham radio operators saw a tornado briefly touch down, producing no damage.
A tornado touched down on the outskirts of Mamou, and damaged 10 to 15 homes near Highway 95 and Fred Street. One home lost its roof. One mobile home was flipped onto the highway.
Hurricane Ike caused category 1 wind damage across Hardin County. Many trees and power lines were downed, some landing on homes and businesses.
Hurricane Ike caused category 1 wind damage across southern Jasper County. Many trees and power lines were downed, some landing on homes and businesses.
Hurricane Ike caused category 1 wind damage across Jefferson County. Many trees and power lines were downed, some landing on homes and businesses.
Hurricane Ike caused category 1 wind damage across Orange County. Many trees and power lines were downed, some landing on homes and businesses.
Hurricane Ike caused category 1 wind damage across Tyler County. Many trees and power lines were downed, some landing on homes and businesses.
Hurricane Ike cuased tropical storm force wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph. This resulted in widespread trees and power lines downed, some landing on homes and businesses.

A 14-15 storm surge at Sabine Pass resulted in the highest water level ever recorded at that location. Any home that was not elevated was destroyed. The storm surge did not top the seawall in Port Arthur, but wave action on top of the surge did. At least 100 homes were flooded in Port Arthur. The surge also backed up Hillebrandt and Taylor Bayou west of Port Arthur, causing widespread flooding in the Hillebrandt, Hamshire, and Fannett communities. The surge also backed up the Neches River in Beaumont, where some homes along the river flooded. In total, at least 4000 homes were flooded county-wide.

A storm surge as high as 10 to 12 feet reached Bridge City and downtown Orange. A 40 year old man died in Bridge City when his truck was washed off Highway 73 near the Rainbow Bridge. Over 8000 homes were flooded.
Several homes on Second Street had water enter them after as much as eight inches of rain fell in a short time.
Lightning struck a church educational building, destroying it.
A cinder block wall of the Acme Refrigeration Company on Empire Drive collapsed due to severe thunderstorm winds.

EF1 Tornado began 1 mile south of the Alexandria International Airport and moved northeast ending along the Red River. Several eyewitnesses watched the tornado cross the tarmac at the eastern end of the airport and damage an airplane hanger. The tornado then damaged several trees and a gazebo before striking a warehouse building in the England Airpark, peeling off its roof. Crossing a golf course, the tornado continued to blow down trees as it passed just a few yards south of a large monument to the US Air Force. The tornado then struck a home on England Drive, blowing away an attached carport that caused partial roof loss of the house. Little damage was noted as the tornado crossed Airbase Drive. Scattered trees were blown down or damaged in neighborhoods both south and north of Highway 1, and a house along Lanny Street had its carport knocked down. Eyewitness reported the tornado crossed the Red River before dissipating. ||This tornado was spawned from a different supercell than the one that produced the Elmer Tornado.

An EF1 Tornado began west of the Calcasieu community and moved northeast ending around 3 miles north of Elmer. Numerous trees were damaged, snapped off, or uprooted all along the path. As the tornado crossed the area around the intersection of Highway 112 and Twin Bridges road, several homes and buildings received minor roof damage. One storage building along Twin Bridges Road was blown 50 yards away and destroyed, but was unsecured to the foundation. A few more homes along Twin Bridges road received minor roof damage before the tornado dissipated in the Kisatchie National Forest. ||The supercell that spawned this tornado later moved across Alexandria and Pineville, producing hail up to penny size and minor wind damage.
Penny size hail was reported by the Red Cross in Pineville.

Up to 3 inches of rainfall fell in 2 hours across the Alexandria & Pineville area during the evening. Earlier in the day, 1 to 3 inches of rainfall also fell across the same area.  The resulting flash flooding affected the same areas that flooded during Hurricane Gustav, including Prescott Road, Wettermark Street, Lee Street, Jackson Street, and the Downtown and Lower Third areas of Alexandria. Some areas in Pineville also saw flooding, including Huntington Drive. Dozens of homes and businesses were flooded, and several cars were stranded in the flooded roadways. Water was up to the hoods of cars in area underpasses, resulting in high water rescues.
Nickel size hail reported at the Highway 29 and Highway 1171 intersection northeast of Ville Platte.

Five to seven inches of rain fell over a five hour period during the afternoon hours across northern Jefferson County. Widespread flooding of roadways was reported by the public and law enforcement in and around Beaumont.  The public reported about a foot of water on Major Drive at Willow Creek Drive in southwest Beaumont, with water covering the yards of area residences.  An NWS employee observed flooding on the frontage roads along Interstate 10 at the Highway 69 interchange, and law enforcement reported several of the underpasses in the city were also flooded.

Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly moving over western and central St. Landry Parish produced five to eight inches of rain in a localized swath from the Evangeline Parish border to just north of Port Barre.  Widespread street flooding was reported in Washington by the local police department.

Showers and thunderstorms repeatedly moving over central and eastern Evangline Parish produced five to eight inches of rain in and around Ville Platte. Several roads were closed due to flash flooding in Ville Platte and in the surrounding rural areas.

A small microburst struck areas 2 miles south of the Alexandria International Airport.  A few trees were blown down in a field south of Highway 28.  Two houses were damaged on Ross Lane, with one house losing part of its roof and another having its carport collapse on a vehicle.  Debris from the first house was thrown across Ross Lane.  A highway department warehouse building had one garage door blown inward and destroyed.  Power lines were blown down in the area.
The public reported penny to nickel size hail in Vidor.
Golfball size hail fell in Vidor.  Reported by KBMT-TV.
Nickel size hail occurred at the intersection of Highway 12 and Farm-to-Market Road 1136.
Penny size hail fell 10 miles southeast of Kirbyville.
Power lines blown down near Highway 105 and Major Drive. Reported by TV station in Beaumont.
Hail up to golfball size accumulated as much as 3 inches deep in Creole.  Reported by Cameron Parish Sheriff Office.
Quarter size hail and estimated wind gusts of 50 mph were reported 10 miles northwest of Pitkin by the public.
Trees were blown down five miles northwest of Ebenezer.

An intense supercell thunderstorm produced a large downburst that began about 1 mile south of Pine Prairie and ended about 7 miles northeast of Ville Platte.  This area of wind damage was around 15 miles long and up to 3 miles wide, affecting the Millers Lake area and the southern portions of Chicot State Park.  Within this zone, scattered trees were blown down from northwest to southeast with several roads blocked by fallen trees.  Power lines were also blown down with a few outbuildings receiving damage to their roofs and siding.  Several above-ground pools and trampolines were flipped over and fences were damaged.  The worst damaged was concentrated around the intersection of US Highway 167 and Old Park Road.  Over 1000 calls of power outages were received by the local electric company.  Winds were estimated around 70 mph.
The public estimated penny size hail fell in Whiteville.
The Vermilion Parish Sheriff Office reported penny size hail fell for around five minutes in Pecan Island.
Quarter size hail was reported in Sulphur by KPLC-TV.
Quarter size hail was reported in Carlyss by KPLC-TV.
Franklin Police Department received several reports of golf ball size hail in Franklin.
Trees were blown down on Harvey Crossing Road northwest of De Ridder in southern Vernon Parish.  Reported by KPLC-TV.

NWS Storm Survey found significant wind damage from a microburst across Dequincy.  One downtown building had its roof blown off and windows were blown out of another downtown building.  A trailer housing an insurance company on East 4th Street also had its roof blown off.  Several other homes and buildings received minor damage to roofs and siding across town. Numerous large trees and power lines were uprooted or snapped, especially in a swath from the downtown area southward to the intersection of the Kansas City Southern railroad tracks and South Grand Avenue.  All damage was in a NNW to SSE direction with winds estimated around 80 mph.
One tree was blown down along Highway 171, 0.5 miles NNW of Gillis.
A carport was blown into a roadway reported by the Beauregard Parish Sheriff Office.
Numerous trees were blown down in Ragley as reported by the Beauregard Parish Sheriff Office.
The public reported several trees were blown down in Oberlin with minor roof damage to a few buildings.
NWS Storm Survey found microburst wind damage along Highway 12 west of the Kernan community.  Numerous trees were blown down from NW to SE in a narrow swath.

NWS Storm Survey found microburst wind damage in the Buhler community along Bankens Road between Highway 27 to Shearing Road.  A 50 foot tall radio tower at a gas plant was toppled and several mobile homes had damage to skirting and siding.  Numerous trees and power lines were blown down.  All damage was in a NW to SE direction with winds estimated around 70 mph.

NWS Storm Survey found microburst wind damage in the Hampton community along Cottongin Castor Road around the intersection with Highway 104.  Numerous large trees were uprooted with one falling on a house.  A mobile home had its roof blown off.  All damage was in a WNW to ESE direction with winds estimated around 70 mph.

NWS Storm Survey found microburst wind damage along a 3 mile long path from 3 miles WSW of Mamou to 2 miles SSW of Mamou.  Along Highway 104 near LD Verette Road several homes received minor damage and outbuildings were blown over.  Numerous trees and power lines were blown down.  Along Highway 13 south of Mamou, two power poles were snapped and several others were blown down.  All damage was in a NW to SE direction with estimated winds around 80 mph.

NWS Storm Survey found major microburst wind damage from 2.5 miles NNW of Lawtell to 2 miles N of Lawtell.  Along Prairie Ronde Highway, several trees and power lines were blown down between Chanteberry Road and Raphael Road.  A convenience store at the intersection of Prairie Ronde Highway and Fontenot Road has its roof partially ripped off with debris blown across the highway into a residence.  All damage in this area was in a W to E direction with estimated winds around 65 mph.||Further east along Bertrand Road, one tied down mobile home was flipped upside down onto several vehicles and destroyed. Debris from the mobile home was blown up to 200 yards away across a field. A large barn adjacent to the mobile home suffered major roof damage. Another nearby mobile home had its roof completely blown off. Other mobile homes in the area received minor to moderate damage, and several outbuildings were damaged or destroyed.  Numerous trees and power lines were blown down throughout the area.  All damage was in a WSW to ENE direction with estimated winds up to 95 mph.

NWS Storm Survey confirms microburst wind damage in subdivisions along and south of Cal Cam Line Road.  Several metal storage buildings were blown over and destroyed.  A metal carport was blown off a home with debris landing on a boat and in yard of residence.  Numerous mobile homes had skirting ripped off.  All damage was in a W to E direction with estimated winds around 70 mph.

NWS Storm Survey found several trees blown down in the southern sections of Lake Charles, stretching from around the intersection of Nelson Road and Ham Reid Road to near the intersection of Gauthier Road and Tom Hebert Road.  All trees were blown down in a NW to SE direction with estimated winds around 60 mph.
A 60 mph wind gust was measured by the Lacassine RAWS Mesonet Station.
A 60.4 mph wind gust was measured at the Lake Charles Ag Center Mesonet Station.
Numerous trees and power lines were blown down throughout St. Landry Parish as reported by the Sheriff Office in Opelousas.
Lafayette Parish Sheriff Office received a report of a tree down in the 6900 block of Landry Road in Duson.
St. Marin Sheriff Office received a report of a tree and power line down on the Atchafalaya River Highway.
The public reported a metal patio was blown off and a barn door blown out on Millcreek Road.
The Bordelonville Fire Department Chief reported trees blown down just east of town.
The Opelousas Daily World newspaper reported the public measured a 62.8 mph wind gust with a Davis Wind Anemometer in Port Barre.

Franklin Police Department and local media reported microburst wind damage along Northwest Boulevard from near Highway 90 to around Yokely Road.  At a truck stop near Highway 90, a tractor trailer was blown over and awnings over the fuel pumps were damaged.  The rear portion of a restaurant was destroyed with debris thrown across nearby fields.  Thirteen utility poles were blown down and a large shed was demolished along Yokely Road.  All damage was in a SW to NE direction with estimated winds around 90 mph.

NWS Storm Survey found microburst wind damage on the north end of Mila Road near the Kings Truck Stop on Highway 190 west of Port Barre. One mobile home was blown off its cinder blocks and completely destroyed.  Another mobile home was also knocked off its cinder blocks and had the roof partially blown off. Debris from both mobile homes blew into a third mobile home causing severe damage to its siding and roof. Two nearby outbuildings were blown over and damaged.  All debris was blown from SW to NE with estimated winds around 80 mph.

NWS Storm Survey found microburst wind damage across Mamou, with the worst damage in the northeastern half of town. A roof was blown off a medical building on the west side of Country Club Lane. Debris from the building was thrown across the road and struck the Savoy Hospital, breaking numerous windows on the third floor and damaging several vehicles in the parking lot. Several homes received damage to roofs and siding, with the patio of one home collapsing.  Numerous large trees and power lines were blown down, with some power poles being snapped off near the ballpark. Power was knocked out to the entire town for nearly 24 hours. All damage was in a NW to SE direction with estimated winds around 80 mph.

Tyler County Sheriff Office reported trees blown down with power outages in Ivanhoe.
Jasper County Sheriff Office reported trees blown down in Buna.

Numerous reports from local media indicate a large downburst with winds estimated up to 80 mph struck the city of Charenton. The roof was blown off the Chitimacha Police Station trailer and a nearby radio tower was toppled. Many flag poles at the Immaculate Conception Church were blown over. The Highway 324 bridge over Bayou Teche received minor wind damage to its wooden beams. Several homes received minor to moderate damage to roofs and siding, and numerous trees and power lines were blown down. Damage was reportedly worse than seen during Hurricane Gustav.

Local media and law enforcement reported a large downburst with winds estimated around 80 mph struck from the Patterson Memorial Airport to the city of Patterson. A tree fell on a home on Highway 182 just west of the airport. One tied-down helicopter was blown over and two tied-down airplanes were flipped upside down at the airport and severely damaged. Numerous trees were blown down in Patterson with some falling on homes. Damage from this storm was reportedly worse than that seen from Hurricane Gustav.
Berwick Police Department and the Morgan City Daily Review newspaper reported the roof of a trailer home was blown off on Arlington Drive in Bayou Vista.

The public reported penny size hail 2 miles west of Toledo Bend Dam.

KFDM-TV and the public reported widespread flash flooding across central and eastern Jefferson County. Several major roadways were underwater in the Fannett and Labelle areas. Numerous roadways and underpasses were flooded in Beaumont, including the intersection of Madison Road and Irving Street. Cars were stalled and submerged in floodwaters on Jimmy Johnson Boulevard between Highway 347 and 9th Avenue in Port Arthur.

KFDM-TV and the public reported widespread flash flooding across Orange County. Several homes in Bridge City and West Orange received minor flooding.

An NWS Employee and local law enforcement reported flash flooding in Lake Charles and Sulphur. Ryan Street and Common Street in Lake Charles were flooded and nearly impassable with water over the curbs. Several streets were also flooded in Sulphur.
The public reported a foot of water covering Highway 182 near Opelousas.

A high-end EF0 Tornado began along Highway 190 west of Krotz Springs and moved northward ending about 3 miles north of Krotz Springs. Trees were blown down at the intersection of Kim Drive and Rainbow Lane. One home had minor roof damage. A barn and workshop were damaged just north of Kim Drive on Highway 105. Several trees were blown over along Highway 105, and a workshop roof was blown off near the end of the path. Path length about 5 miles with path width around 100 yards.

An EF1 Tornado with a path length of just over a half a mile and path width of 50 yards moved across the LeBlanc subdivision west of Catahoula. The tornado began in a field near the intersection of LD Drive and Higginbotham Road with large tree branches blown down and debris thrown into trees. Moving east-northeast, the tornado continued across the subdivision where it damaged numerous houses and mobile homes. One mobile home was flipped at least two times and completely destroyed, and a camper trailer was blown upside down onto a car. The tornado exited the subdivision into an open field east of Estates Avenue. ||In total, 23 homes were damaged or destroyed.  One woman carrying an infant was hospitalized with a spinal injury when she ran from her mobile home to a nearby house and was struck by flying debris.  Two other individuals received minor injuries including facial lacerations.

Damage to the store forced it to close for several weeks.  The tornado continued to the northeast and crossed a Walmart parking lot, flipping over four vehicles and damaging dozens of others.  Further to the northeast, the tornado struck Parkdale Mall, damaging the roofs of several department stores.  The tornado lifted in the east parking lot of Parkdale Mall before reaching Highway 69. |Numerous photographs and videos of the tornado were taken.

Cameron Parish Sheriff Office reported a tornado southwest of Grand Chenier. Radar indicated the tornado was likely a waterspout that moved onshore. No damage was reported.

An EF0 Tornado began south of Pom Roy Road and moved north-northeastward, damaging several trees. As the tornado crossed Highway 14 about 4 miles west of Lake Arthur, it damaged several more trees at homes on the south side of the highway and blew around some outdoor furniture. The tornado then continued north-northeastward across rural areas, knocking down a power pole on Highway 380 and blowing down a swath of sugarcane along Rouch Road. A resident of Thornwell photographed the tornado as it traveled through this area. More power poles and power lines were blown down as the tornado crossed Lyons Road just south of Guidry Road. The tornado then curved northward and north-northwestward, crossing back over Lyons Road just north of Mouton Road, where it knocked down several more power poles before dissipating.

The same supercell that spawned the tornado near Lake Arthur produced a large, long track multiple vortex tornado that touched down south of Highway 90 just east of Farm Supply Road to the southeast of Roanoke. The tornado moved to the north-northeast and crossed Highway 90 around 2 miles east of Roanoke, it produced a half-mile wide damage path along the highway. In this area, a farmhouse received minor damage to the roof, a barn was moderately damaged, and a metal silo was destroyed. In addition, a few trees and several large tree limbs were blown down, and several wooden transmission power poles were snapped in half.  ||Continuing northward, the tornado then passed across Interstate 10, blowing an 18-wheeler and several cars into the median of the highway, and knocking down a few trees. The driver of the 18-wheeler was injured and required hospitalization, and the eastbound lanes of the interstate were closed for several hours. An NWS employee located 1 mile east of the tornado took photographs and video as it crossed the interstate. Further to the north, several trees were blown down along Aaron Road and Dave Williams Road, and the metal roof of a home on Koll Road was blown off. After crossing Grand Marais Road just west of Elton Drive, the tornado damaged the carport of a home and severely damaged a barn. ||The tornado then began moving north-northwestward, blowing down a few trees along Bryan Road and Ardoin Road, before crossing Highway 102 about 2 miles west of Hathaway where it blew down more trees. Curving more northward, the tornado then began moving along Highway 395, where it blew down trees along both sides of the highway and caused minor damage to the roof of one home on Bucklin Road.  Continuing northward through the community of China, the tornado finally dissipated to the north of China Cemetary Road, just west of Highway 395.

Another large tornado touched down about 3 miles south of Elton to the east of Highway 395 as the previous tornado began to dissipate to the west. This tornado damaged a shed along Dan Buller Road, before moving northward and striking Elton. A 3 block wide swath of damage resulted in the western portion of the town, generally between Washington Street and Henderson Street. Numerous large trees and power lines were blown down, with a few trees falling on houses. Several homes received minor roof damage, with a few poorly constructed homes and mobile homes losing their entire tin roofs. Some streets were completely covered with debris from homes and trees. The sporadic nature of the damage was indicative of a multiple vortex structure to the tornado. In total, fifteen homes were damaged in Elton, with four homes completely destroyed. Local officials stated the damage was considerably worse than seen from Hurricane Rita. After leaving Elton, the tornado continued northward into Allen Parish.

The large tornado that moved through the town of Elton in Jefferson Davis Parish crossed into Allen Parish. Continuing northward, the tornado caused scattered damage to trees before dissipating north of Clarence Road.

The same supercell that spawned the tornado that struck Elton produced another brief tornado that damaged a barn on Robert Sonnier Lane, approximately 6 miles north of Elton. Area residents reported the damage to KPLC-TV.

The same supercell that spawned the previous tornado produced another weak tornado that formed south of Ward Road and just west of Deshotel Road. This tornado moved to the north-northeast, causing minor tree damage along Ward Road.  The tornado then moved through inaccessible forested areas east of Norris Road, before reaching the far eastern portions of Oakdale. Several large tree limbs and a few trees were blown down along Highway 372 and South Street in Oakdale before the tornado dissipated just south of Highway 10.
An NWS Employee witnessed several trees blown down in the northern portion of Lake Arthur along Highway 14, with power knocked out to the entire town.
An NWS employee reported several road signs blown down along Interstate 10 at mile marker 71 just south of Egan.
Rapides Parish Emergency Manager reported numerous trees and power lines blown down all across Rapides Parish.

Storm spotters and the Lake Charles American Press newspaper reported widespread street flooding across the central and northern portions of Lake Charles.  Several major roadways were flooded, including Ryan Street and Enterprise Blvd., as were numerous side streets including Granger Street and Franklin Street. Photos showed water was up to the doors of homes on Franklin Street.

An NWS employee conducting storm surveys observed numerous flooded roadways across rural areas of southern Jefferson Davis Parish between Interstate 10 and Highway 14. Some roadways that were underwater and impassable included Farm Supply Road, Lyons Road, Roche Road, and Guidry Road.

KALB-TV and the Alexandria Town Talk newspaper reported significant flooding across Alexandria and Pineville. Several underpasses across Alexandria were flooded, with high water in many ditches and culverts across Pineville. A 12 year old boy playing on his bicycle in a drainage ditch near the intersection of McDermott and Fairbrook Streets in Pineville was swept away by the fast current, and died two days later in an Alexandria hospital.

Morgan City Daily Review reported widespread street flooding across the cities of Patterson, Berwick, and Morgan City. Several streets were closed in Berwick due to the flooding. Photos of flooding on Sixth Street at Belanger Street in Morgan City showed water well above roadside curbs and into the yards of residences. A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers rain gauge at Berwick Locks measured a total of 4.25 inches of rain.

Abbeville Meridional newspaper reported widespread street flooding across the city of Abbeville. Numerous streets were underwater across the city, including Prairie Street, and some roads were closed due to the flooding, including Lafayette Street. Water completely surrounded several homes along Lafayette Street.

Lafayette Daily Advertiser newspaper reported widespread street flooding across the city of Lafayette. Some major roadways such as Verot School Road were underwater, with water up to the undercarriages of some cars. Several coulees across the city also overflowed their banks.
KFDM-TV and the public reported widespread street flooding in downtown Beaumont and Port Arthur.
A CoCoRaHS observer in Westlake measured 1.52 inches of rain in 30 minutes.
The Lake Charles Regional Airport ASOS measured 2.00 inches of rain in 31 minutes.
The Lake Charles Regional Airport ASOS measured 3.97 inches of rain in 2 hours.

Several NWS employees, the Louisiana Department of Transportation, Calcasieu Parish Sheriff Office, and local media all reported major flash flooding across this cities of Sulphur, Westlake, and Lake Charles, and in adjacent unicorporated areas to the south and east of the city. The worst flooding occurred along the Common Street/Gulf Highway corridor eastward to Highway 27 to the south of Highway 14.  In this area, numerous homes were flooded and many roadways were underwater for several hours. As rainfall ended late in the evening across the area, floodwaters subsided across the city but increased across unicorporated areas further to the south as waters drained toward the Gulf of Mexico.||Several flooded homes were reported in southeast Lake Charles on Sundale Drive at Common Street, near Kayouchee Coulee and Highway 14, and on South Meadowlark Drive at Corbina Road.  Numerous major roadways and their adjacent side streets had one half to one foot of water covering them, including Jackson Street in Sulphur, Common Street between Petro Point Drive and Gauthier Road in Lake Charles, Enterprise Blvd. near St. Louis High School in Lake Charles, and Airport Road near the NWS Lake Charles office. Several vehicles were stranded in high water on Tom Hebert Road south of Tank Farm Road to the southeast of Lake Charles, causing the roadway to be closed. The Calcasieu Parish Sheriff Office reported a total of 12 high water rescues across the parish due to vehicles being stranded in floodwaters.

An NWS storm survey indicated flooding from heavy rainfall on October 26th continued for much of the day on October 27 across areas between the Lake Charles Regional Airport and Highway 27. In this area, several roadways were closed for much of the day due to at least one foot of water covering the roadways, including Ward Line Road between Gauthier Road and Tank Farm Road, and Tom Hebert Road south of Tank Farm Road.

Vernon Parish Emergency Management, the Vernon Parish Sheriff Office, and the public all reported widespread flooding of roadways across central Vernon Parish due to persistant moderate to heavy rainfall that began late on October 29th and continued into October 30th. Many streets across Leesville had a half foot of water on them. Several cars stalled in the high water on Highway 171 in Leesville and on Jean Chapel Road near Fort Polk. Many roadways across the area were closed for much of the day on October 30th.

Beauregard Parish Emergency Management reported that a total of 15 roads were flooded across the western part of the parish and were closed for much of October 30th. Five of the roadways remained closed into October 31st.

Beauregard Parish Emergency Management reported that 5 roadways remained closed due to flooding from the heavy rainfall earlier in the day, and continued to be closed into the morning hours on October 31st. As floodwaters continued to drain towards the Sabine River, rising water along Brushy Creek during the morning hours on October 31st washed a car off Friendship Road around 1 mile east of the Bancroft community.

Vernon Parish Emergency Management reported some hunters were trapped by rising waters on the Sabine River from a combination of heavy rainfall the previous day and water releases from Toledo Bend Dam. The hunters had to be rescued.
