Devall Towing reported a wind gust of 40 MPH in the Calcasieu River Ship Channel. The thunderstorm was moving north across Cameron Parish and into Lake Charles.

Scattered thunderstorms moved into Lake Charles with very heavy rainfall. The heavy rain flooded some streets and roadways with a few becoming impassable. One such road was Louisiana AVE at Interstate 210. The highest rainfall rates were estimated by radar to be 2 to 3 inches per hour and rain fell for an hour or two.

Thunderstorms trained across Moss Bluff, Sulphur, Westlake, Topsy, and surrounding areas for multiple hours. Cars began to stall and one water rescue of an elderly lady was reported by midnight. Rainfall totals of 15.63 inches in Gillis and 14.77 three miles north of Moss Bluff were reported as 24 hour totals by 3 AM on the 21st. Across Moss Bluff, Westlake, Sulphur, and Gillis areas many houses and vehicles flooded. Flooding was especially noted along Indian Bayou, Marsh Bayou and near canals as water attempted to drain. The east and west forks of the Calcasieu River from Old Town Bay to Sam Houston Jones State Park also quickly rose as water drained.
A co-op observer measured 14.04 inches of rain for a two day total. Of the 14 plus inches, 8.96 inches of rain fell from 9 pm on the 20th until 7 am the next morning.

Thunderstorms trained across far west sections of Jefferson Davis Parish and the adjacent area of Calcasieu Parish for multiple hours. The majority of the flooding occurred in nearby Calcasieu Parish; however prolonged heavy rain still caused flooding along the head waters of Marsh Bayou at the parish border. Multiple houses along Marsh Bayou from Gillis to Topsy flooded.
Heavy rain from Magnolia Springs to Mountian Union produced minor flooding of roadways.
Heavy rain around the Spurger area produced minor flooding of roadways. The radar estimated 2 to 9 inches of rain in the area.
Heavy rain from slow moving thunderstorms caused street flooding around Newton forcing Law Enforcement to close some roads in and around the city.

Heavy rain in training thunderstorms fell across Tyler County and neighboring Jasper County for multiple hours. Near 6 inches fell during the event. High rainfall rates produced quickly rising water that flooded some streets around Woodville and briefly flooded the lower portion of one home with an inch and a half of water. Minor flooding was also reported at Wolf Creek at Highway 96.

Heavy rain from training thunderstorms fell across Jasper County and neighboring Tyler County for multiple hours. This produce flooding across the region as near 6 inches of rain fell. The high rainfall rates caused flooding around the city of Jasper closing streets, flooding of at least one car, and flooding a couple of houses.

Heavy rain across the Beaumont area produced flooding along Eastex Freeway from near the Highway 287/69/Interstate 10 spilt to Highway 105 in Beaumont. Flooding caused the exit ramps and frontage roads to be impassable to some cars with lower sitting vehicles flooding.

Heavy Rain caused minor flooding of some roadways around Batson including FM770 and around Luberton including Candlestick Drive. Pictures were also sent in via Facebook of minor flooding around Lumberton.
Heavy rain caused minor flooding of FM 1745 at Russel Creek and at Billiums Creek in the Chester area.
Heavy rain from training thunderstorms produced the flooding and closure of numerous county roads along Big Cow Creek between Newton and Call.
Several trees and many tree limbs were blown down or broken around Groves. One tree fell on a house.

The tornado began south of West Round Bunch Road near Susan Circle and traveled generally west and crossed Highway 87/73 south of Cow Bayou. The tornado then turned northwest to parallel Highway 87/73 after crossing the bayou and moved across FM 1006 and lifted before reaching Western AVE. The tornado was strongest before crossing Highway 87/73 and produced EF1 damage to homes and trees. EF0 damage was done after crossing 87/73. Roofs, carports, sheds and trees were damaged along the path.

The tornado began near County Road 303 west of Highway 96 and traveled northwest. The tornado then continued across Highway 96, but dissipated before reaching Marshall Lake just east of County Road 302. Along the path many large pine trees were downed or snapped with some falling onto homes. Also along the path, one building was pushed about 25 feet off of its blocks.

A tornado touched down southwest of the corner of Sandy Lane and Butler Lane well south of Dequincy. The tornado moved west to northwest where it became its strongest along Wanda Lane where EF1 damage was produced. The path continued across highway 27, across Holbrook Park Road, and finally dissipated before reaching Beckwith Creek. Mostly tree damage was noted along the path, however along Edith and Wanda Lanes fence damage was noted along with 3 large trees snapped and roofing was removed from an outbuilding.

A weak tornado touched down in the marsh and woods north of Graywood Parkway and traveled west across Big Lake Road. The tornado then continued down L. Ogea Road and Sancess Road before dissipating. Mostly tree damage was noted along the path, however one home had minor damage and 2 sheds were destroyed.

A strong wind gust from a passing line of storms flipped one shed, damaged a few small trees, damaged one roof of a mobile home, and destroyed one carport along Tall Sky Drive, Rustic View Drive, and Wisperwind Drive.

A weak tornado touched down along the east end of Hoffpauir Road and moved across Highway 171. The weak tornado dissipated near the intersection of Newt Hodges Road and Foreman Road. Only minor tree damage was noted along the path.

A tornado began around 6 tenths of a mile west of Highway 171 along Camp Edgewood Drive and traveled northeast. The tornado continued across Highway 171 and peaked in intensity from the intersection of Gaytline Road and Coanie Jackson Road to Jack's Circle while crossing the curvy Gaytline and Foreman Roads multiple times. The path continued northeast and dissipated near Parish Road 152/Texas Eastern Road near Boggy Creek. Many large trees were snapped or damaged with some falling onto homes along the path with many structures receiving roof damage, especially where the tornado peaked at an EF1. Awnings and gutters were also damaged along with sheds destroyed.
A weak tornado formed south of Highway 190 and dissipated on the north side of the roadway. The tornado only damaged trees along the path.

A weak tornado developed near Highway 13 in the community of Easton. The path continued east parallel to Ardoin Cemetery road before turning northeast and dissipating. Several trees were snapped or damaged along the path.

A video sent to the NWS via Facebook showed a tornado briefly touching down in a rural area of Acadia Parish. A NWS survey team traveled out to the site and found a short path of a weak tornado that damaged a few trees and one above ground pool when a branch fell. The tornado path began along the south end of Ray Lejeune Road and went northeast dissipating before reaching Highway 97.
A report was relayed from KLFY to the NWS of 5 to 6 trees downed and a shed destroyed in the Sunset area from a passing line of storms.
A report was received of a funnel cloud near Bayou Chicot State Park. This funnel cloud was likely associated with the same parent storm that produced a tornado near Easton.
KPLC TV7 relayed that minor flooding was occurring along Parish Road in Moss Bluff. No road closures were noted.

Heavy rain from slow moving storms produced flash flooding in portions of Fort Polk. This caused Birds Creek to quickly rise closing some roadways. Water levels along the creek rose to around 2 feet over roads closing the road into the early morning of November 1st.

Heavy rain from slow moving storms produced flash flooding in portions of Fort Polk during Halloween. This caused Birds Creek to quickly rise closing some roadways. Water levels along the creek rose to around 2 feet over roads closing the road during the morning of October 31st and lasted into the early morning of November 1st.
A fast moving tornado touched down in the Harmony community, blowing down and snapping several large hardwood trees, one of which hit a parked car.

A fast moving tornado touched down near FM1746, blowing down or snapping off several trees. While it was crossing FM92, it ripped off part of the metal roof of a small rural grocery store. Eyewitnesses saw the tornado at the Corp of Engineers office across the street. The sheet metal from the roof was blown into the COE park and damaged several picnic areas, and snapped off several more trees.

A fast moving tornado touched down in a field near Mt. Union, and ripped a well built carport/garage that was attached to a house. While part of the carport roof landed on the home, some of the metal debris was thrown for 200 yards across the field.

A homeless woman in Opelousas was found dead after spending a cold night outside. The low temperature at KLFT, which is 23 miles south of Opelousas, during the morning of the 7th was 20 degrees. The woman refused to go to a shelter the previous evening and was found by a firefighter the next morning behind a fire station.

An Opelousas woman was found dead near Ville Platte after becoming missing a few days prior. The elderly woman suffered from dementia, but she died from exposure. Video shows the woman entering the park alone the day before. The low temperature at nearby KLFT was 20 degrees.

Snow flurries and light rain began during the late afternoon of the 23rd but changed over to freezing rain during the evening. Sleet and light freezing rain continued through noon the next day with freezing drizzle remaining into the afternoon. Ice accumulation reached around one quarter of an inch early in the morning of the 24th with sporadic power outages reported by 4AM. By sunrise most of lower Cameron Parish was without power. Ice accumulation reached between 0.1 to near 0.5 across the eastern sections of Cameron Parish with the highest totals in the northern sections.

Snow flurries and light rain began during the late afternoon of the 23rd but changed over to freezing rain during the evening. Sleet and light freezing rain continued through noon the next day with freezing drizzle remaining into the afternoon. Ice accumulation reached around one quarter of an inch early in the morning of the 24th with sporadic power outages reported by 4AM. By sunrise most of lower Cameron Parish was without power. Ice accumulation reached between 0.1 to near 0.4 across the eastern sections of Cameron Parish with the highest totals in the northern sections.

Snow flurries began in Calcasieu Parish during the late afternoon of the 23rd, but soon changed over to light freezing rain after sunset. Traffic accidents began during the early morning hours of the 24th with one being fatal as all bridges in the Parish became iced and eventually closed. A large portion of the parish received around 1/4 of an inch of ice accumulation; however some southern sections received more as the transition to sleet and snow never occurred. All schools and public offices were also closed due to icing on area roadways.

Light freezing rain and a few flurries began very early on the 24th with bridges and overpasses becoming iced over a few hours later. One traffic accident became fatal in Welsh from slippery roads. All bridges were closed by around 8AM and remained closed for most of the day. Ice accumulation across the parish ranged from one tenth to around 1/4 of an inch.
Light freezing rain fell across the north half of Vermilion Parish from early on the 24th through the afternoon. The accumulation of ice was generally at one tenth of an inch or less.

Light freezing rain began during the morning of the 24th and did not end until the afternoon. All overpasses and bridges were reported closed by 9:45 AM CST in Iberia Parish as ice had already lead to multiple traffic accidents. Ice accumulation ranged from near 0.1 to around one quarter of an inch.

Freezing rain began during morning of the 24th and did not stop until the afternoon across Saint Mary Parish. Ice accumulation ranged from around one tenth of an inch or less along the coast to between one third to around four tenths of an inch. All bridges were closed across the parish during the event.
Freezing rain began during the morning of the 24th and lasted into the afternoon. Ice accumulation ranged from around one quarter of an inch to around four tenths of an inch.

Sleet and snow began across Beauregard Parish during the evening of the 23rd. Mostly snow fell across the northern portions of the parish with around 2.5 inches recorded. Across the southern portions a mix of freezing rain, sleet, and snow fell. Snow and sleet accumulation across the southern sections totaled around half an inch while ice accumulation totaled between 0.1 to two tenths of an inch.

Sleet and snow began across Allen Parish during the evening of the 23rd. Mostly snow fell across the northern portions of the parish with around 2.75 inches. Across the southern portions a mix of freezing rain, sleet, and snow fell. Snow and sleet accumulation across the southern sections totaled around half an inch while ice accumulation totaled between 0.1 to two tenths of an inch.

Freezing rain spread into Acadia Parish during the late evening of the 23rd and gradually changed over to sleet and snow in most of the parish during the morning of the 24th. Ice accumulations ranged from around one tenth to near a quarter of an inch across the parish with sleet and snow accumulations ranging from around half an inch across the central sections to around one inch across the northern portions.

Freezing rain spread into Lafayette Parish during the late evening of the 23rd and gradually changed over to sleet for portions of the parish during the morning of the 24th. Ice accumulations ranged from around one tenth to around a quarter of an inch across the parish with sleet accumulations generally around half an inch.

Freezing rain spread into northern portions of Saint Martin Parish during the late evening of the 23rd and gradually changed over to sleet for portions of the parish during the morning of the 24th. Ice accumulations ranged from around one tenth to around a quarter of an inch across the parish with sleet accumulations generally around half an inch or less.

Freezing rain and flurries began across Evangeline Parish during the evening of the 23 and soon transitioned to all snow. Ice accumulation across the parish was less than one tenth, however snow totals ranged from around one inch in the south to 2.5 inches in the north.

Freezing rain and flurries began across Saint Landry Parish during the evening of the 23 and transitioned to snow and sleet. Ice accumulation across the parish was around one tenth of an inch or less, however snow totals ranged from around half an inch in the south to around 2 inches in the north.

Sleet moved into Vernon Parish during the evening of the 23rd, however precipitation soon changed to snow. Snow kept falling through the night and into the morning of the 24th. Snow accumulation ranged from around 2.5 inches to around 3.5 inches.

Sleet moved into Avoyelles Parish during the evening of the 23rd, however precipitation soon changed to snow. Snow kept falling through the night and into the morning of the 24th. Snow accumulation ranged from just below 2 inches to around 3 inches.

Sleet moved into Rapides Parish during the evening of the 23rd, however precipitation soon changed to snow. Snow kept falling through the night and into the morning of the 24th. Snow accumulation ranged from just below 2.5 inches to near 4 inches. All bridges and overpasses along Interstate 49 were closed as well as bridges across the Red River during the event and into the night following the event.

Sleet moved into Tyler County during the evening of the 23rd, however precipitation soon changed to snow. Snow kept falling through the night and into the morning of the 24th. Snow accumulation ranged from 1.5 inches to 2.5 inches.

Sleet and freezing rain moved into Hardin County during the evening of the 23rd. Precipitation in the northern sections of the county changed over to snow, however farther south freezing rain remained common. KPLC-TV 7 reported that some of the worst flooding of the area occurred around Laccasine where roadways were closed and some residents were temporarily unable to leave their homes. At least one home was flooded during the event.

Numerous vehicles were flooded along area roadways and one house was also reported flooded during the event. Flood waters almost entered buildings in downtown.

Multiple hours of heavy rain produced flooding across a large portion of Calcasieu Parish, but mainly south of Interstate 10 in Lake Charles. The first reports of flooding to the NWS were of people Kayaking in the streets near La Grange HS, and soon many reports of flooded streets with stalling cars were being received. Water entered some homes and some apartment building across the southern sections of city as well. The KLCH ASOS received 6.94 inches from the event which set a record for the day besting the previous record set by Tropical Storm Allison in 1989, however radar estimates were up to around 8 inches in the event.

A tornado touched down in rural Jefferson Davis Parish near Thornwell. It was videotaped by several people. The tornado touched down on Goose Island Road where it blew trees down. When it crossed Highway 14 it damaged a small barn and several trees. The tornado paralleled Highway 99 as it moved north remaining over mostly crawfish and rice fields. A couple of power lines were bent and one was snapped. A larger barn was destroyed along Highway 99 and several more trees snapped. A modest amount of rain fell across the area during the 17th into the early morning of the 18th with the New Iberia area receiving between 1 and 3 inches. Heavy rain began during the morning of the 18th as a slow moving cold front moved in producing an additional 3 to 6 inches. The rain began to flood roadways by mid morning forcing their closure. Rain began to fall across Lafayette during the 17th and into the early morning of the 18th with 1 to 3 inches across the parish as a cold front moved closer. The water level at Sabine Pass rose to 3 feet above MLLW and peaked out at 3.81 feet around 40 minutes later. The water level from Sabine Pass to Johnson Bayou and Pelican Beach rose to cover the beach, however the surf did not cause damage as it was generally contained by the dunes. Farther east to Long Beach and Constance Beach the water completely covered the beach and moved onto the neighborhood roads in spots. There are spotty dunes along this stretch. Some minor road damage was noted and debris was moved onto some roadways. At Holly Beach water completely surged across the coastal ridge. Water reached a depth of 2 feet deep along portions of highway 82 just west of Holly Beach. Several Campers, sheds, and some vehicles were damaged by the fast moving flood waters. Some residents were awakened by waves hitting their campers and called the local police department for help. A couple of pets were also drowned at one residence. The water level at Calcasieu Pass rose to 5.83 feet above MLLW around one hour after reaching 3 feet.

The water level at Cameron rose to 3 feet above MLLW just before 2 AM CST as a line of storms approached. Around one hour later and when the line of storms moved by the water level quickly spiked to 5.83 feet above MLLW. Flood water from the Gulf of Mexico poured into the town of Cameron. Streets flooded and dumpsters and out building were displaced. One bar received around one inch of flood water. Farther east at Rutherford Beach residents were awakened by waves crashing into their campers. Some residents floated in their campers while calling the local police department. Several campers were damaged along with sheds and vehicles. The road from Creole to Rutherford Beach was under water for a couple of days while the marsh drained.

The water level along the coast of Vermilion Parish rose to around 3 feet above MLLW after midnight on the 23rd as a line of storms approached. The water level held generally steady through 3 AM before quickly rising to 5.98 at the Freshwater Locks NOS site by 4 AM. Major flooding of the coastal area occurs at 6 feet above MLLW. The tide quickly receded after peaking. Water in Vermilion Bay remained at 3 feet or above through sunrise. No report of damage was received from Vermilion Parish.

A line of thunderstorms moved into the Southeast Texas and Southwest Louisiana Coast during the early morning of the 23rd. While the larger water rises occurred in Louisiana where the stronger storms were the gulf still reached minor flood stage at Sabine Pass. The water level quickly rose to 3.81 feet above mllw and then quickly fell back below flood stage 10 to 15 minutes later.

A report was received of hail to 0.75 inch in diameter northeast of Abbeville.

A spotter southeast of Lafayette reported around 70 feet of wooden fence blown down with metal support poles for the fence bent around 20 degrees off the ground. A few shingles were a blown off a near by house as well as a few large branches broken along Presbytere Parkway.
A report with a video of 1.25 inch hail was received from Tulla through Facebook. Another report a couple minutes later reported hail to 2.5 inches in the same town.
A report of hail to two and a half inches in diameter was received from a severe thunderstorm in Bordelonville.
A report of hail measuring 2 inches in diameter in Sugartown.
Penny size hail was reported in Jennings from a passing thunderstorm.
A report of penny size hail was received from Evangeline during a thunderstorm.
Media relayed a report of 1.25 inch hail near Opelousas.
A few hours of moderate to heavy rain produced minor street flooding in and around the city of Lake Charles.

events.event_narrative: The tide station at Calcasieu Pass recorded wind gusts of 38 and 40 MPH during a thunderstorm.
A severe thunderstorm produced hail to one inch in diameter in Kirbyville.

A tornado touched down near FM highway 1013 west of Spurger and snapped the tops of several pine trees off. When the tornado moved to County Road 4394 two homes received minor damage to the roofs with some shingles taken off. Several trees were snapped near the base of them and a couple of sheds and barns had some metal roofing material peeled off. The tornado caused more damage to two more homes on County Road 4375 where roofing shingles or tin were partially blown off the homes, carports, and garages. More trees along this road were also snapped at the base facing north. The tornado dissipated shortly thereafter. This same storm produced the tornado in Jasper County in the Rock Hill Community.

The tornado began just south of the intersection of County Road 301/Brewster���s Road and Highway 96 where small tree branches and an awning were broken. The path of the weak tornado continued along the path of Brewster���s Road breaking small branches before peeking out near the homes at the end of the road. The tornado reached peak intensity as it passed one home destroying a portion of the home, mainly the garage. It also damaged or destroyed 3 outbuildings near the home and downed or snapped many large pine and oak trees. The tornado continued east-northeast across a field and destroyed another carport and removed portion of an outbuilding`s roof. Four vehicles were damaged or destroyed between the two homes. The tornado then dissipated in the forest.
Multiple trees were reported down along Highway 96 near Browndell.
Strong north winds at the coast pushed the tide to 1.1 foot below mllw at Sabine Pass and at the Rainbow Bridge at the north end of Sabine Lake.

Strong north winds along the coast pushed the tide at Calcasieu Pass below 1 foot below MLLW during two consecutive low tides. The first low tide fell to -1.25 MLLW and the second fell to -1.1 below MLLW. The tide also fell across Calcasieu Lake with the Lake Charles Bulk Terminal briefly touching -1 foot below MLLW.

Strong north winds along the coast pushed the tide at Calcasieu Pass below 1 foot below MLLW during two consecutive low tides. The first low tide fell to -1.25 MLLW and the second fell to -1.1 below MLLW. The tide also fell across Calcasieu Lake with the Lake Charles Bulk Terminal briefly touching -1 foot below MLLW.
Strong north winds behind a cold front pushed the tide to less than 1 foot below MLLW. The tide gauge at Fresh Water Lock recorded a tide of -1.27 below MLLW at low tide.
Lightning struck a home of a Southeast Texas doctor setting the roof on fire. Firefighters were able to extinguish the blaze after a neighbor reported it. No one was injured in the fire.
KALB TV relayed a report of quarter size hail near the Boyce/Gardner area via Facebook.
The Highway 8 bridge in Boyce across the Red River closed during the morning of the 24th until the ice melted. Max accumulation was measured at 0.06 at the KAEX ASOS and 0.02 at KESF.
Light freezing rain accumulated to a total of 0.005 at Oberlin before the ice melted. No travel problems were reported.
The tide at Calcasieu Pass fell to -1.52 below mean lower low water while stiff north winds occurred behind a cold front.
The tide at Calcasieu Pass fell to -1.52 below mean lower low water while stiff north winds occurred behind a cold front.
The tide at Freshwater Lock fell to -1.59 below mean lower low water while stiff north winds occurred behind a cold front.
Due to strong north winds at the coast the tide fell below -1 below mean lower low water for 3 hours reaching -1.21 during the event at Sabine Pass.
The water level at Cameron fell below -1 below lower low water for three and a half hours reaching -1.36 during the event.
The water level at Cameron fell below -1 below lower low water for three and a half hours reaching -1.36 during the event.
The water level at Freshwater Lock fell below -1 below lower low water for three hours and 45 minutes hours reaching -1.55 during the event.
The water level at Sabine Pass fell below -1 below lower low water for two and a half hours reaching -1.12 during the event.
The water level at Cameron fell below -1 below lower low water for two hours reaching -1.17 during the event.
The water level at Cameron fell below -1 below lower low water for two hours reaching -1.17 during the event.
Pictures and reports from Facebook indicated around half an inch of snow and sleet fell across Leesville.

Sleet and snow fell across Rapides Parish during the morning of the 5th. Alexandria International Airport and surrounding areas received one quarter inch of accumulation. During and after the event the Highway 8 Bridge in Boyce was closed for several hours from icing.
Around half an inch of snow and sleet fell across portions of Avoyelles Parish including Marksville and Bordelonville. Accumulation information was received through Facebook.

Thunderstorms trained across portions of Hardin County from near Sour Lake to Lumberton during the morning of the 12th. While rainfall rates were not excessive, several hours of moderate to heavy rainfall flooded some secondary roads, a section of FM 421 at a low water crossing, and one home in west side of Lumberton.

Thunderstorms trained across Jefferson County for several hours during the 21st. Jimmy Johnson Blvd, Nall street, and Highway 365 were a few of the streets that were flooded during the event. Numerous reports of cars being stalled due to high water were received as a result of the street flooding.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms trained across Orange County for multiple hours. This flooded and closed several roadways around Bridge City.
Heavy rain from thunderstorm trained across Jefferson and Orange Counties and western Calcasieu Parish for multiple hours. This caused flooding around the town of Vinton and closed some streets.

Tide stations and river gauges from Cameron and the Calcasieu River show tide levels fell below 1 foot below MLLW during the morning of the 5th and did not rise above -1  until the morning of the 6th in Calcasieu Lake. The tide at the coast did rise above -1 during high tide. The water level fell to -2.16.

Tide stations and river gauges from Cameron and the Calcasieu River show tide levels fell below 1 foot below MLLW during the morning of the 5th and did not rise above -1  until the morning of the 6th in Calcasieu Lake. The tide at the coast did rise above -1 during high tide. The water level fell to -2.16.

North winds drove the tide at the coast below one foot below MLLW during the morning of the 5th. The tide did rise above -1 during high tide only to fall back below during the next cycle, however the strong winds kept Sabine Lake below -1 during the whole event. The tide level fell to -1.47 at its lowest point.

A thunderstorm developed over South Lake Charles during the early afternoon. As the storm grew a funnel cloud developed just north of the Lake Charles Regional Airport. Numerous National Weather Service employees watched the funnel as it drifted east.

A slow moving thunderstorm developed over South Lake Charles and produced heavy rainfall. Flood water flooded at least one home on Sundale Drive near Common Street. Numerous roads were flooded along with cars stalled along Prien Lake, Derek, Kirkman, and Sale Roads and Streets. Storm Total from the event at the Lake Charles Regional Airport was 5.04 inches most of which fell in one hour.

Numerous cars stalled across Iberia Parish, but mainly in New Iberia during the heavy rain and flooding event. Numerous streets also closed and some schools dismissed early. Some roads remained closed for several hours.

Heavy rain caused many streets to flood across portions of Saint Mary Parish during the morning of the 14th. Many streets were closed for several hours while the water slowly drained. Some area schools dismissed early during the event.

Heavy rain caused many roads to flood with up to one foot of water across portions of the Alexandria area. Media passed along a report of two cars under water at an underpass at Jackson Street. Flood waters also entered a furniture store and a few homes in Alexandria.
Heavy rain across northwest sections of Avoyelles Parish closed several state highways.

events.event_narrative: A wind gust of 40 MPH was measured with a passing storm 7 miles southwest of Johnson Bayou.
Six to nine inches of rain fell flooding State Highway 105 between Bevil Oaks and Sour Lake. The flooded roadway was reported by a NWS employee.

Multiple roadways in Jefferson County, but mainly near Nome and Central Gardens were closed after several inches of rain fell during the evening of the 16th. Some of the roadways included in the closure were FM 365, 1406, and 366 along with Highway 347.

A tornado developed in the southern sections of DeRidder near the intersection of Highway 27 and Bon Ami Street. The tornado continued along a northeast path damaging trees until becoming stronger before crossing Highway 190. Damage along Highway 190 included roofing and siding removal to multiple structures. The tornado collapsed an awning at the East Village Shopping Center north of Highway 190 before dissipating.
Golf ball sized hail reported in the west side of Leesville.
Spotters and the public reported 1 to 1.25 inch hail from Tioga to Ball in Rapides Parish.
Golf ball sized hail was reported on the north side of Pineville with a passing storm.
Multiple public reports of one inch hail was received from near Deville during a passing storm.

A decaying thunderstorm passed southeast across the Jefferson County coast in Southeast Texas and into the near shore gulf waters of Cameron Parish. A heat burst occurred to the north of this storm across southern and central sections of Calcasieu Parish. Wind gusts of 45 to 55 MPH were common with a one second gust of 74 MPH recorded on top of the Magnolia Building in Downtown Lake Charles by KPLC 7. The ASOS at the Lake Charles Regional Airport recorded 51 MPH and Chennault Field recorded 54 MPH. Many trees were downed in the city as were power lines. Mostly light damage was noted to some structures with one dock at a city park damaged from wave action on Prien Lake. After the event some sections of the city were with out power for 3 days.

A decaying thunderstorm passed southeast across the Jefferson County coast in Southeast Texas and into the near shore gulf waters of Cameron Parish. A heat burst occurred to the north of this storm across north and northeast sections of Cameron Parish. Wind gusts of 45 to 55 MPH were common. Trees and power lines were downed across northern Cameron Parish from the event. Mostly light roof damage was noted to some structures. After the event some areas were with out power for 3 days.

An EF1 tornado originated near the Neches River west of Kirbyville and moved east to southeast crossing Highway 82 west of Kirbyville near the airport. The tornado continued into Newton County between FM 1013 and South Saint Aubin Road. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along the path damaging a few homes from debris hitting them. Some outbuildings were also damaged. The average width was 50 yards and the path was 8.27 miles long in Jasper County. The total length of the path was 13.3 miles.

This tornado formed near the Neches River west of Kirbyville in Jasper County and moved east to southeast. The tornado entered Newton County between FM 1013 and South Saint Aubin Road as it passed north of Call. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along the path damaging a few homes from debris hitting them. Some outbuildings were also damaged. The average width was 50 yards and the path was 5 miles long in Newton County. The total length of the path was 13.3 miles.
A tree was blown onto a house in Spurger.
A 24 inch in diameter tree was blown down in a 60 MPH wind gust during a thunderstorm.
Law enforcement reported trees blown down in Call.

An EF1 tornado began Southeast of Call and moved across mostly forest. The tornado snapped or uprooted many trees along its path before crossing the Sabine River and moving into Beauregard Parish west of Bancroft. The tornado crossed the Sabine River near the east end of Magnum Road. The tornado path in Newton county was 3.94 miles long and 50 yards wide.
Media relayed a report of quarter size hail in Singer.
Quarter size hail was reported in Breaux Bridge.
A report of baseball sized hail was received from between Breaux Bridge and the Parks Area.
Several photos were received of tennis ball to baseball sized hail from Catahoula.
A storm over Hayes produce quarter sized hail.
The emergency manager of Beauregard Parish reported trees down between Fields and Ragley.
An NWS employee reported trees and power lines down along Clark Road off of Highway 12.
Photos of tree damage along Highway 110 between Singer and Longville was received through social media.
Local media received and then relayed a photo of a power pole snapped along Highway 171.
Media relayed a report of a tree down in Reeves.
Trees were downed between Reeves and Kinder along Highway 190.
The Louisiana State Police relayed a report of two tractor trailers overturned on Interstate 10 near mile post 108 in Breaux Bridge. Also near by a trailer home was destroyed by wind.

An EF1 tornado formed in Newton County and moved east to southeast across the Sabine River. The tornado passed near Bancroft before dissipating near Fields. Mostly tree damage occurred along the path, however one home was damaged when a tree fell onto the roof and a couple of outbuildings were also damaged near Bancroft. The path in Beauregard Parish was 8.36 miles long with a total path distance of  12.3 miles. The average width was 50 yards.
A spotter estimated a wind gust of 65 MPH northwest of Breaux Bridge.
The Saint Landry Police Department reported a tree down on Highway 103 near a high school.
A tree was reported down on Charlie Field Road.
A passing line of thunderstorms downed power lines and several trees around Leesville.
A tree was blown down along Highway 27 in Dequincy.
Trees reported down around Evans.
A NWS employee reported several trees and power lines down from DeRidder to Singer along Highway 27. Also, a bar suffered roof damage between DeRidder and Rosepine.
Media reported trees down in Pitkin and around much of Beauregard Parish.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Kinder.
Nickel sized hail was reported in Elton.
Power poles were blown down between Ville Patte and Bayou Chicot.
The police chief of Vinton estimated a wind gust of at least 60 MPH.
A roughly 12 inch in diameter live oak was blown over in Hackberry. The picture of the downed tree was received through Facebook.

A power pole was downed near SJ Welsh Middle School. Trees and power lines were downed across the city of Lake Charles with some portions of the city out of power for around 2 days after the line of storms passed.
A roof was removed from a trailer home in Lebleu Settlement.
Trees were reported down in Mamou and across the rest of the parish as well.
A wind gust of 64 MPH was recorded by the LSU Ag Center in Crowley. The Acadia Police Department also reported several trees down around Crowely and also in Rayne.
A spotter estimated winds were near 60 MPH with a passing line of thunderstorms. A tree was also reported down on power lines in Lafayette with the tree on fire.
The Saint Landry Police Department reported a tree down on Grant and South Main Street in Breaux Bridge.
A tree fell onto Interstate 10 blocking the west bound traffic over the Atchafalaya Basin.
A power pole was downed onto a house in Maurice.
A tree was blown down onto highway 87, and another was blown down in Franklin.
A tree with other debris was blown onto Chitimacha Trail.

One inch in diameter hail was reported in Beaumont.
One inch in diameter hail was reported near Fred.
One and a quarter inch hail was reported northwest of Kirbyville.
A photo was received through social media of one and a half inch hail southeast of Magnolia Springs.
Golf ball size hail was reported in Port Acres.
A report was relayed by Beaumont media of penny to quarter sized hail in Nederland.
A spotter estimated a wind gust around 60 MPH.
The Hardin County Sheriffs Department relayed a report of numerous trees and power lines down in Lumberton.
A photo of one inch diameter hail was received through social media.
The Jasper County Sheriffs Department reported numerous trees down on power lines and cars county wide.
The Hardin County Sheriffs Department reported numerous trees down county wide.
The Tyler County Sheriffs Department reported trees down from Woodville northwest along Highway 287.
Photos of trees and large branches down on a car near Buna was received through social media.
The Sheriffs Sheriffs Department of Orange County relayed a report of a tree down on FM 1131 and one tree on a house.
The Newton County Sheriffs Department reported trees and power lines down county wide.

The EF1 tornado developed between FM 255 and County Road 228 snapping several trees in the area of Lowe Road and County Road 227. There was damage to at least two residences when trees fell onto homes, sheds, and vehicles. The tornado then continued to the northeast crossing Highway 96 and County Road 200 causing tree damage.  When the tornado reached County Road 207 it hooked more to the north northeast snapping several trees. At one residence on County Road 207 a tree fell onto a shed completely destroying the shed. The tornado dissipated somewhere in the wooded area between County Road 207 and County Road 205 in northern Jasper County. The average path width was 80 yards and the length was 3.6 miles.

A decaying thunderstorm passed southeast across the Jefferson County coast in Southeast Texas and into the near shore gulf waters of Cameron Parish. A heat burst occurred to the north of this storm from Calcasieu and Cameron Parishes into central sections of Jefferson Davis County. Wind gusts of 45 to 55 MPH were common with the highest wind gust of 63 MPH recorded at the Jennings Airport. Trees and power lines were reported down in the parish.

Several inches of rain caused Mill Creek to rapidly rise. A truck was swept off County Road 200 at Mill Creek and driver had to be rescued.
A tree fell onto a home and into the utility room and a bedroom in Jeanerette.
Beaumont media received multiple photos from along the Eastex Freeway, Delaware Street, Lucas Drive, and other Northeast Beaumont roads that were flooded. Several cars were flooded during the event.
Flooding from thunderstorms closed Ida Wells and Lee Bridge Roads around Holloway and also flooded Jackson Street and other roads in Alexandria.
A wind gust of 49 MPH was recorded at Cypremort Point with a thunderstorm.
Multiple pictures were received from a weak tornado that developed over a field near Iota. No damage was caused by the tornado as it dissipated quickly in the same field.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced heavy rain across Beaumont for a few hours. This combined with already full ditches and wet ground produced street flooding on multiple roadways. Flood waters also approached some homes along Euclid Street, and cars were stalled in under passes near Lamar University.

Numerous streets and intersections were flooded in and around Lake Charles and slow moving storms produced 2 to 4 inches over the city. Several roads became nearly impassable including Tank Farm, College, Prien Lake, and Luke Powers.
Beaumont Media relayed a report of quarter size hail in Lumberton.

Heavy rain trained across portions of Southeast Texas for multiple hours on already saturated soil. This produced flooding around Beaumont which closed some streets including an underpass along MLK Boulevard and stranded at least one motorist on a feeder road of the Eastex Freeway.

Heavy rain trained across Southeast Texas including Hardin County for multiple hours. This occurred on already saturated soil and produced flooded roads which closed some for several hours. At least one home in Sour Lake had one inch of water in the structure.

Heavy rain trained across the southern sections of Jasper County for multiple hours. This occurred on already saturated soil. 12 to 15 inches of rain fell around Buna and multiple high water rescues had to be preformed. Many roads were flooded out with some vehicles being swept off the roads. Many houses, businesses, and churches flooded in Buna and a few in Kirbyville with several inches of water. Flood waters also filled a commercial oil vat which overflowed causing a small spill in Buna.

The heavy rain and flash flood event from the 17th lingered into the early morning of the 18th. Flood waters remained across southern sections of Jasper County through the morning of the 18th with many roadways remaining closed as the water slowly drained.
Heavy rain trained across southern and central sections of Newton County for several hours on already saturated soil. This produced roadways that were flooded out and closed for many hours.

Heavy rain during the 17th produced flash flooding in south and central sections on Newton County. Multiple roads remained closed from Bon Wier to the southwest into the 18th as flood waters slowly drained.

events.event_narrative: A resident of Sabine Pass reported water going over the roads around Sabine Pass at the time of high tide including Highway 87 from the Intracoastal Waterway to the town. The surrounding coastal marsh was also flooded.

A persistent onshore flow drove water levels to a foot or two above normal levels. At high tide and while a line of thunderstorms passed through the area water covered Highway 82 near Holly Beach in a few sections.

A persistent onshore wind drove waters levels along the coast to a foot or two above normal. As a line of thunderstorms moved through the area at high tide water covered portions of Marshal Street in downtown Cameron.

A persistent onshore flow drove water levels a foot or two above normal levels,  however a line of thunderstorms pushed through during the afternoon of the 25th lifting them higher. The tide gauge at Freshwater Lock hit 6 feet with the passing storms. The operator of the lock said the tide actually hit 6.8 feet on the gulf side of the lock and quickly receded. The high water flooded the  marsh, the yard around the lock, and nearby docks.

Pictures posted to social media showed streets around Cypremort and Burns Points flooded around the time of high tide. Tides were driven up even more when a line of thunderstorms pass through the area.
Heavy rain produced flooding near and north of Trout Creek. The Newton County 911 Call Center reported water over Highway 82.

events.event_narrative: A weather station on a rig installed by Beaumont media recorded a sustained wind of  50 MPH with a gust of 61 MPH as low pressure pushed east across the coastal waters.

Heavy rain moved into Hardin County early during the morning of the 31st. Flooding of roadways with water at least 2 feet deep was reported in Silsbee by 6:15 AM. By 10:51 AM the Department of Highways reported that most roads in the county had water covering them and water rescues were ongoing by 11 AM according to the county police department near Silsbee and Kountze. Around 50 houses in the county were flooded. By the end of the event Reeves Elementary in Silsbee received 9.0 inches, Kountze Elementary received 9.71 inches, 11.58 inches was reported from West Hardin High School in Saratoga, and 14.25 reported at Highway 105 at Pine Island Bayou near Batson.

Heavy rain moved into Jasper County early in the morning of the 31st. Flooding was reported along County Road 784 near Buna by 7 AM. Numerous roads were reported flooded through the rest of the morning in different sections of the county with some being impassable especially at low water crossings. A COCORAHS report from near Kirbyville reported 7 inches of rain during the morning.

Heavy rain moved into Newton County during the morning of the 31st with flooding first reported at 9:17 AM with water covering Farm to Market 1004 near Call. Numerous other roads were flooded during the morning and early afternoon with some becoming impassable.
Heavy rain lingered over the City of Orange for a few hours. High rainfall rates produced significant street flooding around the city.
Multiple trees were blown down between Mount Union, Magnolia Springs, and Kirbyville. A metal roof was also blown off of a house with a few other utility buildings damaged during a thunderstorm.
Trees and utility poles were reported down northeast of Newton along with a roof blown off a storage building.

The tornado began 7 miles west northwest of Sugartown and caused damage mostly to trees. The tornado reached peak intensity  as it crossed Lone Star Church Road were it snapped several trees and a utility pole. It also damaged two car canopies and broke several large tree branches along the path before dissipating 5 miles south southwest of Cravens.

The Vernon Parish 911 Call Center reported water across Highway 171 in Rosespine a little after 7 AM. Heavy rain continued to fall for most of the morning producing additional flooding across a large portion of the parish. Most of Fort Polk had flooding on roadways around the installation. Several roads, highways, and parking lots were also reported flooded and closed into the afternoon.
Heavy rain from a slow moving line of thunderstorms produced flooding around DeRidder. Numerous roads were flooded and closed from late morning into the afternoon.
Trees were blown down and the roof was damaged to a carport in Gillis.
A wind gust of 61 MPH was recorded at Fort Polk.
Trees were reported down along highway 107 in Pineville.

The tornado formed in the swampland between Highway 112 and the Calcasieu River. The tornado crossed LA 461 causing damage to trees. Along Elmer Road a house had roof damage. The wide path continued northeast damaging many trees. One house was crushed by a falling tree. The tornado dissipated near the Claiborne Range.
A report was received a mobile home that was tied down blown off its blocks. A carport was also damage and trees were downed.
Heavy rain from a slow moving line of thunderstorms flooded and closed several roads in the western sections of Rapides Parish from late morning through early afternoon.

As rainwater drained toward Pine Island Bayou and Black Creek flooding continued in south portions of Hardin County for a few days. Around 15 homes flooded in Pinewood Estates while Pine Island Bayou crested.

Strong north winds in the wake of a strong low pressure system and cold front pushed water levels below normal along the Cameron Parish coast. The tide at Cameron briefly touched 1 foot below MLLW at 7:09 AM CST.

Strong north winds in the wake of a strong low pressure system and cold front pushed water levels below normal along the Cameron Parish coast. The tide at Cameron briefly touched 1 foot below MLLW at 7:09 AM CST.

Heavy rain fell across portions of Saint Martin Parish flooding and closing roadways. A rainfall total of 6.16 inches was reported from Saint Martinville via Cocorahs.
Closed streets and highways from flooding was reported from Beaumont, Central Gardens, Port Arthur, and Groves.
Heavy rain fell across southwest sections of Orange County. This caused flooding over southern sections of Vidor flooding and closing roadways.
The Calcasieu Parish Sheriffs Department reported a tree down across railroad tracks in DeQuincy.
The Evangeline Parish OEP reported several roofs of out buildings damaged along with windows blown out and small trees down from a passing storm northeast of Mamou.

A 50x20 foot piece of sheet metal on a wood frame was torn off a garage and thrown approximately 350 feet, an RV garage was bent, three south facing garages were bent inward, a fence was bent to the ground, a utility pole was bent, and boats were blown off of trailers and into a fence.

This tornado began along highway 112 where it uprooted some trees. It crossed the Calcasieu River and damaged the roof of one home and a barn on East River Road, as well as uprooting several trees. When it reached Peniel Loop Road it flipped a travel trailer where a man was inside. He was transported to a hospital for injuries. Several more trees were uprooted in the Peniel Loop Road area before the tornado dissipated.

The tornado touched down near Highway 71 less than a mile north of LSU Alexandria downing a tree onto a garage destroying it. Several mobile homes received minor damage. A car also had a tree fall on it. The tornado dissipated near Highway 1 where several more trees were uprooted. The tornado was visually seen and photographed by several people.

An EF-1 tornado touched down in a sugar cane field near highway 90...and was on the ground for 2.6 miles before it dissipated in another sugar cane field near highway 87. In between 2 businesses and 28 homes were damaged. One restaurant lost most of its flat metal roof, several mobile homes lost most of their metal roofs, and a few homes were knocked off their pilings. Other homes had windows and sheet metal damage...as well as garages and carports. Many trees were snapped and at least 20 telephone/power poles were snapped as well.

Multi day rainfall amounts of 5 to 20 inches fell across Newton County with the most falling late on the 9th and early on the 10th. Most roads experienced flooding with many closed in the northern sections of the county, and several roadways were washed out.  Several homes were also reported flooded during the event with at least one high water rescue of an elderly lady. Road damage alone was estimated at $1.5 million.

Multi day rainfall amounts of 4 to 12 inches fell across Jasper County with the most falling on the 9th and 10th. Many roads experienced flooding with many closed.  Multiple rescues were done during the event with people trapped inside flooded homes in Kirbyville and other towns. Around 136 homes had minor flooding, 82 had major flooding, and 5 were destroyed. Thirteen businesses also received major flooding damages. Most of the flooded structures were around Kirbyville.
Four to eight inches of rainfall fell during the morning of the 10th causing water levels to quickly rise. This flooded roadways and around 33 homes.

Multiple reports of flooded and closed roadways was received from Hardin County during the heavy rain event. The heaviest rain fell on the 10th when 3 to 6 inches of rain fell in the morning. At least 9 homes were flooded.

Heavy rain resulted in flooded streets around the Beaumont area. All underpasses in the city were flooded and closed. Poorly drained roadways like MLK Boulevard near Lamar University was also flooded.
Heavy rain across north and west portions of Orange County produced street flooding. This closed some streets in the Vidor area.

Heavy rain fell during the 9th and 10th with over 10 inches of rain falling during the 10th. Widespread flooding was reported in Northwest Vernon Parish. Roads were closed and some were washed out. A couple dozen homes were flooded during the event.

Three to five inches of rain in a fairly short period of time on already saturated soil produced flash flooding in portions of the Alexandria area. The flooding closed some streets and flooded some structures including Pheonix Magnet School.

Prolonged heavy rain on the 9th and 10th pushed Toledo Bend Reservoir to record levels while flooded creeks and streams flowed into the Sabine River. This pushed the river level at Burkeville to a record of 53.82 feet which was 5.77 feet higher than the previous record set in 1999. At Bon Weir the new record set on the 13th was 0.71 feet higher than the previous record set in 1913. At Deweyville the new record set on the 15th was 1 foot higher than the previous record set in 1884. Along the river numerous structures were flooded or in some cases, washed away. The hardest hit town was Deweyville where nearly every structure was flooded to some degree including the schools. County-wide, 458 homes received minor flood damage, 350 had major flood damage, and 500 homes were destroyed by the flood. Ten businesses received major flood damage. At least 60 million dollars is estimated to be the damage totals for homes and businesses, with an additional 26 million dollars for public property.

Flood water from heavy rain on the 9th and 10th gradually flowed down the Sabine River to Orange County. The river at Orange crested on the 17th at 7.62 feet. This was 2.24 feet below the record set during Hurricane Ike in 2008 and was the second highest crest recorded. Areas north of Interstate 10 had much higher levels since the freeway and railroads acted as a damn holding back water. Most homes along the river flooded with some taking several feet of water, especially north of I-10. Roughly 1,500 structures were affected during the event with 190 structures flooded which includes 177 residences. This caused an estimated $2 million in damage to public infrastructure and roughly $4.4 million to private structures.

Water quickly rose along the Sabine River on the 10th as flood water flowed into the basin from Toledo Bend and from the area tributaries. The river set a record crest on the 11th of 53.82 feet at Burkeville which was 5.77 feet above the previous record set in 1999. Areas along and west of Louisiana Highway 111 were flooded with the worst hit community being Evans were almost every home flooded, some were flooded to the roof tops. Around 400 structures were reported flooded with around 200 considered majorly damaged or destroyed in Vernon Parish. Highway 8 near the river was heavily scoured with the south side of the road collapsing near the stateline. The bridge across the river was still closed more than 2 months after the flood with the supports undermined.

Flood water from the heavy rain event on the 9th and 10th pushed down the Sabine River. The river stage at Bon Weir crested on the 13th. The record crest was 0.77 feet above the previous record that was set in 1913. Flood waters reached to Louisiana Highways 111 and 389 and nearly completely covered areas to the west of the roadways. This pushed water into the town of Merryville. Around 300 structures were flooded.

Flood water from the heavy rain event on the 9th and 10th pushed into western sections of Calcasieu Parish flooding areas generally along and west of Highway 109. This flooded sections of Starks and Vinton. The river stage at Deweyville crested at one foot higher than the previous record crest set in 1884. An estimated 319 structures were flooded.
A strong onshore flow kept tides above normal for multiple cycles. The tide level peaked at 3.4 MLLW during the morning of the 10th at Sabine Pass.
A strong onshore flow kept tides at the coast above normal for multiple cycles. The tide peaked at 3.6 MLLW at the high tides during the morning and evening of the 10th at Cameron.
A strong onshore flow kept tides at the coast above normal for multiple cycles. The tide peaked at 3.6 MLLW at the high tides during the morning and evening of the 10th at Cameron.

The water level at Freshwater Lock pushed above 4 feet MLLW during the early morning of the 9th and went above 4 feet for multiple tide cycles through the 11th. The tide peaked at 4.76 MLLW during the early morning of the 11th.

The tide at Amerada Pass pushed above 3 feet MLLW from a persistent onshore flow early on the 10th and remained high through multiple tide cycles. The tide peaked at 3.75 MLLW during the morning of the 11th.
A strong onshore flow pushed the tide above 3 feet MLLW for one tide cycle before a cold front pushed through the region. The tide peaked out at 3.54 MLLW late in the evening of the 30th.
A strong onshore flow pushed the tide above 3 feet MLLW for one tide cycle before a cold front pushed through the region. The tide peaked out at 3.54 MLLW late in the evening of the 30th.

The tide level at Freshwater Lock pushed above 3 feet MLLW during the evening of the 30th and fell during the morning of the 31st behind a cold front. The tide peaked at 4.81 MLLW shortly before midnight on the 30th.
The strong onshore flow pushed the tide level above 3 feet for a few hours during the night of the 30th. The tide peaked at 3.25 MLLW before midnight.
Heavy rain from the 9th and 10th pushed the Neches River into flood. Several structures were flooded along the river between Silsbee and Evadale.
Heavy rain during the 9th and 10th pushed the Neches River into flood. around 10 structures downstream of Steinhagen Lake flooded.
Heavy rain during the 9th and 10th caused the Neches River to flood portions of Southwest Jasper County. Around 25 structures were flooded during the event.
The flood wave from the heavy rain event during the 9th and 10th moved across western sections of Orange County flooding around 10 homes.

The flood wave traveled down the Red River from North Louisiana flooding areas between the main levees. An estimated 154 structures were flooded. The railroad tracks at Boyce also became impassable at the peak of the event. Also, a water control structure along Bayou Darrow in Grant Parish failed sending water into far northwest sections of Rapides Parish. Areas along Rigolette Bayou also flooded.
The flood wave from the heavy rain event in North Louisiana pushed down the Red River flooding areas between the main levees in Avoyelles Parish. An estimated 38 structures were flooded.

Heavy rain during the 9th and 10th drained into the upper reaches of the Calcasieu River in Rapides Parish. This produced the 2nd highest crest on record, and only 1.1 feet below the record set in 1953 at Glenmora. This flooded roadways near the river and affected around a dozen structures with one flooded.

The flood wave from the heavy rain event during the 9th and 10th moved down the Calcasieu River flooding structures near Oakdale and Oberlin. At Oakdale 30 homes flooded, 2 flooded at Oberlin, and 3 flooded at Indian Village.

TXDOT reported Farm-to-Market 366 AT SH 347 flooded in Jefferson County closing portions of the roads. Over 5 inches of rain was reported during the event by several gauges in the county.

Water flooded Farm-to-Market 253 closing portions of the road.

Allen Parish 911 reported portions of highway 190 closed due to flooding between Reeves and Kinder.

Flooding was reported along Ambassador Parkway at multiple intersections. Flood waters was also reported entering a high school auditorium at the peak of the event.

Widespread tree and power line damage occurred around Woodville. Many trees had large branches broken or were up rooted. The vast majority of the trees fell to the east. One mobile home had a tree fall onto it just west of Woodville and the occupant was injured when the tree fell. A building near the intersection of Highway 69 and North Charlton had roofing material removed along with windows blown out.
Numerous trees and power lines were downed across Hardin County.

Lake Rayburn Fire Department extracted an individual that was pinned in bed by a fallen pine tree. The person was transported to a nearby hospital. The Jasper AWOS also reported a wind gust of 54 MPH when the line of storms passed.
A picture was posted to social media showing a tree fell on a truck in Kirbyville.
Numerous trees were downed around Jasper. One tree fell onto a house near College and 2nd Street.
Multiple trees were downed around Van Buren Elementary and nearby streets in Groves.

The tornado touched down southeast of Woodville near highway 287 where tree fall displayed greater convergence and some roofing material was removed from a building. The tornado continued to the southeast snapping numerous softwood trees before dissipating just East of County Road 4250.

The tornado began near FM 1005 just north of Magnolia Springs where it uprooted several pine trees. A home along FM 1005 was damaged when a tree fell on it. The path continued northeast and caused mostly tree damage with minor out building damage also noted. The tornado dissipated near Boggy Creek north of CR 317.

A tornado developed approximately 10 miles southwest of call along county road 702 and moved northeast along county road 1004 snapping or uprooting numerous trees and power lines over a wide swath. The tornado destroyed a single wide trailer just west of us Highway 96. The trailer flipped over twice with three residents inside. One was person was transferred to the hospital to receive stitches. The other two victims sustained only minor injuries. An aluminum shed near the trailer was lifted and thrown approximately 200 yards. The tornado then crossed us Highway 96 where it continued to snap or uproot trees and power lines before dissipating approximately 1 mile south of call in Newton County.
Several trees were downed along FM 1004 near Highway 96.
A tornado cut a path of over 9 miles through Jasper County before dissipating south of Call. Damage in Newton County was confined to minor tree damage along Holmes Road.
Numerous streets were flooding around Silsbee and Kountze including Highway 92.

KALB Meteorologist Adam Burniston went to the site and sent pictures of tree damage including up rooted trees and large branches broken. An outbuilding was also damaged. Many vehicles were also flooded during the event with some being swept into a drainage ditch near Bank Street close to Downtown Lake Charles. The flooding also flooded several homes and at least one business in Lake Charles. Several people had to be rescued from their flooded vehicles. Streets in Sulphur and Westlake also became flooded. Lake Charles Regional Airport set a daily rainfall record with 5.20 inches and 3 to 6 inches of rainfall was common from Vinton to Iowa. The highest amount reported in the parish was near Chenault Airport at 9.37 inches.

Numerous roadways were flooded during the event as well including Highways 69, 190, and 256 near Woodville.

This flood wave traveled down the Neches flooding areas south of Dam B including some homes in the Barlow Lake and Sheffields Ferry Communities.

Heavy rain during the end of May produced flash flooding across areas upstream of B. A. Steinhagen Lake. Even one small earthen dam failed near Colmesneil. This flood wave traveled down the Neches flooding some roadways just east of Silsbee.

Heavy rain during the end of May produced flash flooding across areas upstream of B. A. Steinhagen Lake. Even one small earthen dam failed near Colmesneil. This flood wave traveled down the Neches flooding areas south of Dam B including some out buildings around Evadale and low lying roadways.

Heavy rain during the end of May produced flash flooding across areas upstream of B. A. Steinhagen Lake. Even one small earthen dam failed near Colmesneil. Flooding occurred along Williamson and Gyther Streets with multiple vehicles stranded. One person was trapped in their vehicle with water above the bottom of the door. The fire department rescued the motorist.
A pedestrian was struck by lightning outside the Westlake Burger King.
Multiple trees down in Iota. One large branch impaled a vehicle.
A mobile home was severely damaged by a fire started from a lightning strike in Youngsville.
Several trees were reported down near Burkeville.

High rainfall rates moved into Orange County during the late afternoon of the 13th. While flooding was generally minor across much of the county, in Vidor roadways were flooded and impassable for a short time including under an overpass of Interstate 10.
The media relayed reports of one trailer flipped and another crushed by a falling tree near Vidor.

Street flooding along Ambassador Caffery and a few other poorly drained streets were first reported during the early morning of the 12th. High rainfall rates continued through the day with many streets being flooded and some structures by mid morning. Widespread flooding of vehicles, structures, and high water rescues began during the late morning across Lafayette Parish. The Vermilion River reached major flood stage by sunrise on the 13th and remained above major flood stage for 5 and a half days. Rainfall totals surpassed 20 inches in the southern section of the parish over the 12th and 13th. An estimated 9,376 structures flooded during the event.

Numerous secondary roads were reported around New Iberia during the morning of the 12th. A vehicle was also swept into a ditch during the morning and numerous evacuations were ongoing by the evening. Rainfall continued through the rest of the 12th and the 13th. Over 20 inches of rain fell over a large portion of the parish. An estimated 3,756 structures flooded during the event.

The Acadia Parish Emergency Manager first reported flooding along a few streets in Eunice during the evening of the 12th. Periods of heavy rain continued for another day with 6 to 10 inches of rainfall reported across much of the parish. An estimated 3,936 structures flooded during the event from either flash flooding or river flooding.

During the evening of the 12th flooding of some roadways started to occur in Saint Landry Parish. The heavy rainfall continued eventually flooding Highway 190 which remained closed for multiple days due to standing water. Water continued to rise into the 13th eventually flooding an estimated 2,878 structures.
Streets began to flood during the morning of the 13th and then structures a couple of hours later as heavy rain kept falling. An estimated 363 structures were flooded during the event.

Local media and law enforcement reported numerous streets were flooded an impassable during the late morning of the 13th. Around Jennings the exit ramps from Interstate 10 were flooded and some sections the interstate itself had water over it. Interstate 10 was closed at Highway 165. An estimated 1060 structures were flooded during the event.

Local law enforcement reported 20 people were being evacuated from flooded homes around Ville Platte. Additional homes were flooded in Mamou. And estimated 1043 structures were flooded during the event.
Many flooded roadways were reported flooded during the heavy rain event. An estimated 1500 homes were also flooded from heavy rainfall.
Numerous roads were reported flooded during the heavy rain with some sturctures taking on water as well. An estimated 22 structures flooded during the event.
Portions of western Saint Mary Parish flooded during the event. Some roadways became flooded and an estimated 103 homes flooded.
A tree was reported down in Alexandria from a passing severe storm.
The sheriff's department reported a tree down across the road near Lecamp.
Numerous streets and structures flooded during the heavy rainfall. An estimated 2481 structures flooded.

Flooding was reported along roadways near Clifton. Some roadways became impassable  during early morning hours near the Calcasieu River. A vehicle was swept away after attempting to drive through high water near Big Creek. A female and child was swept down stream. The small child was found clinging to a tree in good condition, however the driver was found nearby already drowned.

Stream gages along the Vermilion River in Lafayette Parish crested during the 15th at the end of the flash flood event. Major flooding along the Vermilion continued through the 24th-25th and kept some neighborhoods flooded for a couple of weeks. At the Surrey Street Gage 10 feet is flood stage and the Vermilion crested at 17.6 feet which is the 2nd highest recorded crest.

The gage at Lake Martin along the Vermilion River crested during the 17th as water drained from Lafayette. Major flooding along the Vermilion continued through the 23rd and kept some areas near the river and lake flooded for a couple of weeks. At the Lake Martin Gage 10 feet is flood stage and the lake crested at 15 feet.

The flood wave moved down the Vermilion River and crested during the morning of the 14th at 13.75 feet. An estimated 2520 homes flooded along the Vermilion River. The River at Perry dropped below major flood stage during the morning of the 18th.

Heavy rain over the northern sections of the Mermentau River Valley gradually worked to Cameron Parish and the coast. The river crested during the afternoon of the 18th on the northeast side of Cameron Parish and dropped through the remainder of the month. Most of the impacts across the area were flooded roadways and marshland,  however 47 structures still flooded.

The flood wave moved down the Mermentau River causing a crest of 10.8 feet at Lake Arthur and at the town of Mermentau. The flood stage is 4 feet, and this was the 5th highest recorded crest at Mermentau. Many roads and structures were flooded or remained flooded along the river into late in the month.

The flood wave moved down the Mermentau River causing a crest of 10.8 feet at Lake Arthur. The flood stage is 4 feet. Many roads and some structures were flooded or remained flooded along the river into late in the month in far west sections of Vermilion Parish.

Heavy rain fell on the 12th, 13th, and 14th and gradually drained into the Mermentau River. Interstate 10 became closed as the river flowed across the roadway from the end of the flash flood event on the 14th through the next few days while the river crested. At the town of Mermentau the river crested at 10.8 feet which was the 5th highest recorded crest. Flood stage is 4 feet. Many roadways and homes stayed flooded for multiple days as the water slowly drained after the flash flood event.

Flooding along Bayou Teche occurred from around Breaux Bridge southward into Saint Mary Parish. In Iberia Parish roads and some structures were flooded by the end of the flash flood event, and some remained flooded for multiple days and the water slowly drained.

Flooding along Bayou Teche occurred from around Breaux Bridge southward into Saint Mary Parish. In Saint Martin Parish roads and some structures were flooded by the end of the flash flood event, and some remained flooded for multiple days as the water slowly drained. Flooding also occurred to the newly built trail head building for the Teche Paddle Trail in Breaux Bridge.

Flooding along Bayou Teche occurred from around Breaux Bridge southward into Saint Mary Parish. In Saint Mary Parish flooding was mainly confined to the northwest section of the parish along the bayou. Some roadways and structures remained flooded for multiple days as the water slowly drained toward the gulf and the Atchafalaya River.
The Calcasieu Parish Emergency Manager reported several streets flooded in Southeast Lake Charles from heavy rain. Some vehicles were flooded with a few roadways having hip deep water.

Several garages and outbuildings were|also damaged or destroyed. Along US Highway 171, several power|poles were blown down with debris on the highway. The peak winds were estimated at 110 MPH.
A tornado briefly touched down on L D Verrette Lane, damaging|three homes. All three had roof damage, with partial metal roofing|material removed. The peak winds were estimated at 75 MPH.
A tornado touched down along Lloyds Bridge Road, damaging several|homes and large barns. Debris was strewn across the adjacent fields. The estimated peak wind was 110 MPH.

A tornado formed over Bunkie and produced widespread tree damage|across Bunkie, especially the western side of town. Two homes|were destroyed when trees landed on them and came through the roof.|At least another 70 buildings were damaged or destroyed in Bunkie. The peak estimated wind speed was 105 MPH.

At least 30 buildings were damaged or destroyed.|Numerous power lines and poles were blown down along major|roads including LA Highway 114 and Main Street. Neighboring strip mall stores|also received minor facade damage and a portable fireworks shop|was destroyed. Across the street, several large trees fell on homes|and several other buildings were damaged as well. The estimated peak wind was 110 MPH.

Some of the|trees landed on homes and caused damage. A barn/garage had part of|its metal roof ripped off. The estimated peak wind was 105 MPH.

A tornado touched down along Boogaerts Road, removing part of|the roof of a single-wide mobile home. A carport was tipped over,|and several trees were snapped. Two other homes received minor|damage from flying debris. The estimated peak wind was 105 MPH.

Light rain changed over to freezing rain then to sleet and snow through the afternoon of the 6th. Accumulations were generally very light, however ice still developed on some roadways and bridges around Alexandria and Boyce. Elevated sections of I-49 and the LA 8 bridge were closed for several hours until the precipitation ended and temperatures rose above freezing.

Rain became freezing rain, then sleet and snow during the afternoon of the 6th. While accumulations were light, patchy ice developed on some roadways including I-49 near Bunkie and northward. The interstate was closed during the evening until the precipitation ended and temperatures rose above freezing.

It knocked a tree down on the edge of|the field, before moving across the field and picking up a deer feed|and watering device. As the device flew through the air, it decapitated|a deer, killing it. The tornado blew part of the tin roof off a a one|story home,and peeled back the carport on the other side of the home.|Several trees in the neighborhood were uprooted or snapped at the trunk. The peak estimated winds were 105 MPH.

Some buildings received roof damage from the tornado. The strongest wind damage occurred at the Immigration Office of the Federal Department of Homeland Security, where a large section of the metal roof was removed. The tornado dissipated a little north of this location. The maximum winds were estimated at 115 MPH. The tornado was 100 yards wide and 3.57 mile long.

A few pine trees were snapped between Glenmora and Forest Hill.|Most damage was medium to small branches. The storm began near McNary Cutoff and|LA 113 and dissipated near LA 112 and US 165. The maximum estimated wind speed was 105 MPH.

The tornado continued|north across Castor Plunge Road where it reached its maximum width of around|half a mile. Many pine trees were snapped or uprooted. The tornado dissipated|near Bayou Boeuf. Most of the path was in the Kisatchie National Forest. This|tornado was seen and filmed by many people in the area. The maximum wind speed was estimated at 120 MPH.

The tornado touched down near US 165 and Bowie Drive, blowing down|several trees, damaging a gas station awning, and blowing the doors in and the|side of a large storage building. Storm chasers filmed a weak tornado on I-49 near Lena. One of|the storm chase vehicles drove through the tornado. No significant damage was|found in the region. Video of this was seen on social media. Max wind speeds were estimated at 60 MPH.

A security video from a car body shop caught a small but intense tornado. The tornado only removed 2 pieces of tin from the shop roof,  however it lifted a car off the ground, spun the vehicle around, and then set it down. The tornado dissipated on Ashy Road. Estimated winds were 100 MPH.

Widespread heavy rain fell across Central Louisiana with amounts ranging from 6 to 10 inches. Many homes in south and west sections of Alexandria along with numerous streets flooded during the event. Flooding was also reported in Boyce and Ball. The debris line from the flood water was noted to be several inches deep in houses across entire neighborhoods during the tornado survey the following day in South Alexandria.

Widespread heavy rain fell across Central Louisiana with amounts ranging from 6 to 10 inches. Numerous roads were reported flooding during the event along with some vehicles. The ASOS sites KBKB and KPOE reported 9.74 and 9.30 inches respectively.

A large swath of 5 to 10 inches of rain fell across Southwest and Central Louisiana during the morning of the 30th. Most of the highest rainfall totals occurred in Northwest Acadia Parish. At least 1 home was flooded in the parish along with numerous streets.

Heavy rain in thunderstorms moved across the portions of Acadiana and flooding streets around Carencro. Water closed many streets and approached neared homes. Swanky's Restaurant in Carencro reported 3 inches of water in the structure.
